title: Who wrote the last message: a harness-termination census of the human-labelled failure-attribution corpora

glossary.failure-attribution corpus: a released set of failed multi-agent runs in which a human marked the responsible agent and the decisive step; attribution methods are trained and scored on it
glossary.harness-terminated run: a run whose final message was produced by the orchestration code or by a provider error path (a content-filter or rate-limit HTTP error, a context-length error, a max-turns notice, a fallback 'FINAL ANSWER' printed by the framework) and not by an LLM call of any agent
glossary.natural failure: a run that failed on its own, as opposed to an injected-failure corpus (Who&When Pro, Aegis) built by replaying a successful prefix and inserting an error
glossary.Wilson interval: a 95% confidence interval for a proportion that stays inside [0, 1] at small counts
glossary.Cohen's kappa: chance-corrected agreement between two readers of the same items

statement: Download the released trajectories of the three human-labelled natural-failure attribution corpora (Who&When, 184 runs; MAST's human-annotated traces; LongRCA Bench, 1,140 runs from five sources) and, with one corpus-format-specific deterministic scanner per corpus, label each run $i$ with $z_i \in \{0, 1\}$, where $z_i = 1$ if the final message's author is a non-LLM code path or the trace carries a provider error string at or after the labelled decisive step with no agent-authored message following it. Report per corpus $c$ the share $h_c = \frac{1}{n_c}\sum_{i \in c} z_i$ with a Wilson 95% interval, the pooled share $h = \sum_c n_c h_c / \sum_c n_c$, and for the flagged runs the cross-tabulation of the human label (orchestrator vs other agent) against the last LLM-authored speaker before the termination. Two readers hand-check a random 40-run sample of flagged and unflagged runs and report Cohen's kappa against the scanner.
claim: At least one in ten labelled runs in the natural-failure attribution corpora ended on a message no agent wrote, so a tenth of the 'agent failures' the attribution field trains and scores on are harness faults.
trick: Read who authored the last line of every failed run the field blames an agent for, and count how often it was the framework or the API error handler.
why_now: 2611.13254 (2026-11-09) ran the scan on one corpus and found 26 of 58 hand-crafted Who&When runs end in a provider content-filter HTTP 400 with a harness-printed FINAL ANSWER, 0 of 126 algorithm-generated runs do, and left 'the same harness-fault scan on MAST-Data, LongRCA or TRAVERSE' open in its own text; LongRCA Bench v4 (2026-08-15) added 1,140 human-annotated natural failures from five sources, the largest such corpus, unscanned.

killing_experiment.design: Step 0 ($0, 1 day): fetch the three corpora's release pages, record trace format, source frameworks and label fields per corpus; reproduce 2611.13254's 26/58 and 0/126 on Who&When with own scanner (a mismatch beyond 2 runs stops the step). Step 1 ($0, 3 days): write one scanner per corpus format (authorship of the final message from the record's role/sender fields; provider error strings: 'content_filter', 'HTTP 400', 'Error code', 'rate_limit', 'context_length_exceeded', 'max_turns', framework fallback strings read from the source frameworks' code); compute $h_c$, Wilson intervals, pooled $h$; cross-tabulate label vs last LLM speaker on flagged runs. Step 2 ($0, 1 day): two readers hand-check 40 runs (20 flagged, 20 unflagged), Cohen's kappa; report false-positive strings (an agent quoting an error) separately. Total: $0, 0 GPU-h, 5 days.
killing_experiment.kills_if: Pooled $h < 0.05$ with the Wilson upper bound under 0.08, and $h_c < 0.05$ on both LongRCA and MAST: the Who&When hand-crafted split is a one-off (one framework, one provider's 2025 content filter) and the claim about 'attribution corpora' is dead; the residue is a footnote re-scoring Who&When. Also dead at step 0 if LongRCA's or MAST's release does not carry per-message authorship (then $z_i$ is not computable and the probe is a sketch).

preregistered_surprise.expected: Judgment probability 0.40 that pooled $h \geq 0.10$; 0.55 that $h \geq 0.05$; expected shape: LongRCA's five sources split, with orchestrator-style frameworks (AG2, Magentic-One-like) at 10-30% and single-agent coding sources near 0; on flagged runs the human label equals the last LLM speaker before the termination in over 70% (the mechanism by which a harness fault becomes an agent's fault).
preregistered_surprise.field_assumes: LongRCA Bench 2608.15242 (abstract, fetched 2026-11-15): '1,140 complete failed trajectories from five sources, all human-annotated for responsible roles and earliest decisive root-cause steps'; 2610.17747 (abstract, fetched 2026-11-15) frames the validity threat to attribution benchmarks as 'spurious signals (surface cues) that predict the annotation', with no non-agent termination category; the card: the Who&When corpus 'attributes those 25 runs to the orchestrator in 4 and to another agent (mostly the web surfer) in 21'.
preregistered_surprise.belief_changing: If $h \geq 0.10$, every attribution accuracy reported on these corpora is scored partly against labels for runs no agent finished, and the corpora need an exclusion rule plus a 'no agent acted' label before the next method paper; if $h < 0.05$ outside Who&When's hand-crafted split, the field learns the contamination is one framework's 2025 artefact and the published numbers on the other corpora stand.

scorecard.target_value: In print: 2611.13254 sec. 4.6 and its open-items list ('the same harness-fault scan on MAST-Data, LongRCA or TRAVERSE; and the effect of the 45% contaminated split on published attribution accuracies'); 2610.17747's call to 'report these tests when developing failure-attribution benchmarks'. Who pays: the attribution-method community (54 arXiv papers in the 12-month window on the conjunction 'failure attribution' AND multi-agent AND LLM, fetched 2026-11-15), the corpus owners, and anyone training a verifier on these labels.

impact_ceiling.floor: A note with $h_c$ per corpus and the label-vs-last-speaker table, cited by the next corpus release and by 2611.13254 v2. Requires steps 0-2. Judgment p 0.6.
impact_ceiling.middle: An exclusion rule and a terminal-message provenance field adopted by one corpus (LongRCA or the Who&When maintainers) and a re-scored accuracy table for the methods evaluated on it. Requires C-W46-02 as well. Judgment p 0.25.
impact_ceiling.ceiling: 'Who wrote the last message' becomes a standard validity test for trajectory corpora (attribution, TRAVERSE-style mistake annotation, MAST-style taxonomies), with a 'no agent acted' category in the taxonomies. Requires the single-agent extension to TRAVERSE and a taxonomy owner's adoption. Judgment p 0.1.

scorecard.relevance: Narasimhan route (tau-family): zero. HAL route: indirect (HAL's archives are not attribution corpora; the provenance rule applies to any trajectory release). Evaluators and benchmark-validity work: direct. Industry: moderate (teams training failure-locating verifiers on public corpora). Jacob's edge (numerics, GPUs, identities): zero; this is a deterministic text audit.
scorecard.kill_probe: Step 1: $0, 0 GPU-h, 5 days; dead if pooled $h < 0.05$ (Wilson upper bound under 0.08) and both LongRCA and MAST under 0.05.
scorecard.density_and_ownership: Occupant of the mechanism on one corpus: 2611.13254 ('26 of 58 hand-crafted Magentic-One runs end in a provider content-filter HTTP 400 ... 0 of 126 algorithm-generated runs'); its authors are the natural owners of the extension. Nearest validity audit: 2610.17747 ('on three benchmarks, simple predictors match or beat GPT-4.1') — cue predictability, not label-object validity. Corpora: Who&When 2505.00212, MAST 2503.13657, LongRCA 2608.15242; injected corpora excluded by construction (Who&When Pro 2607.09996: 'injects a failure only after exactly replaying a successful prefix'; Aegis 2509.14295: 'adaptively inject context-aware errors into successful execution trajectories'). Density on the harness-fault conjunction (provider/harness error words AND agent AND trajectories AND failure/attribution): 11 total, 1 direct (the card), fetched 2026-11-15; the attribution-method conjunction: 54 in the window. Kill-search role words: label noise, annotation noise, trace quality, spurious cue, benchmark contamination, infrastructure error, fallback answer, termination reason, exception, timeout, max turns, invalid trajectory, data cleaning.
scorecard.why_now: 2611.13254 posted 2026-11-09 with the scan on one corpus and the open list; LongRCA v4 2026-08-15. Flag: the method is a string scan; the enabling piece is the released corpora, not a technique.
scorecard.register_and_not: Benchmark-validity measurement with a protocol consequence (an exclusion rule and a provenance field). It is not a new attribution method, not an annotation study of agent behaviour, and not a claim about why agents fail.

title: Re-scoring attribution on the runs an agent finished: Who&When accuracies with the 26 harness-terminated runs held out

glossary.agent-level accuracy: the share of failed runs for which a method names the human-labelled responsible agent
glossary.step-level accuracy: the share for which it names the labelled decisive step
glossary.contaminated split: the 26 hand-crafted Who&When runs that 2611.13254 found end in a provider content-filter error with a harness-printed final answer
glossary.last-speaker baseline: a rule that blames the agent whose message immediately precedes the run's terminal message

statement: Take every published per-run prediction on Who&When that a method's release carries (step 0 enumerates the releases of the methods in the 2026 attribution literature, starting with the Who&When paper's own baselines), and recompute agent-level and step-level accuracy on (a) the 26 harness-terminated hand-crafted runs, (b) the 32 remaining hand-crafted runs, (c) the 126 algorithm-generated runs, with Wilson intervals; report the change $\delta_m = \mathrm{acc}_m(\text{clean}) - \mathrm{acc}_m(\text{all})$ per method $m$. Alongside, score the last-speaker baseline on (a) and (b): if it reaches the human label far more often on (a) than on (b), the contaminated labels are a recency artefact a trained method can learn. Zero model calls.
claim: Published Who&When agent-level accuracies move by more than their reported margins when the 26 runs no agent finished are held out, because on those runs the human label is the last speaker and methods that learn recency are paid for it.
trick: Score the attribution methods only on runs an agent actually finished, and check whether 'blame whoever spoke last' explains how they scored on the rest.
why_now: 2611.13254 (2026-11-09) states 'the effect of the 45% contaminated split on published attribution accuracies' as open; the contaminated set is now enumerable by a deterministic scan.

killing_experiment.design: Step 0 ($0, 1 day): list which attribution papers released per-run predictions on Who&When (releases, not tables); if none does, the probe falls back to the baselines reproducible at zero cost (last-speaker, random, all-orchestrator) and to the label table alone. Step 1 ($0, 2 days): recompute accuracies on splits (a), (b), (c) for every released prediction set; Wilson intervals; last-speaker baseline on (a) vs (b). Total $0, 0 GPU-h, 3 days.
killing_experiment.kills_if: For every released method, $|\delta_m| \leq 2$ points on agent-level accuracy and the last-speaker baseline scores within 10 points of the same on (a) and (b): the contamination does not move the published numbers and the labels on the contaminated runs are not a recency artefact; the probe is a footnote. Also dead at step 0 if no method released per-run predictions and the Who&When paper's own baseline outputs are unavailable (then only the baseline arm runs and the claim about 'published accuracies' is unsupported).

preregistered_surprise.expected: Judgment probability 0.45 that at least one released method's agent-level accuracy moves by more than 3 points when (a) is held out; 0.6 that the last-speaker baseline matches the human label on more than 60% of (a) against under 35% on (b).
preregistered_surprise.field_assumes: 2610.17747 (abstract, fetched 2026-11-15): 'A high score should mean the judge checked the faulty step against the run'; the Who&When corpus labels (card: 'the corpus attributes those 25 runs to the orchestrator in 4 and to another agent (mostly the web surfer) in 21') are treated as ground truth by every method paper in the 54-paper window.
preregistered_surprise.belief_changing: If accuracies move, the Who&When leaderboard of attribution methods is partly an artefact of a 2025 content filter; if they do not, the contamination is a corpus-hygiene note and the published rankings stand.

scorecard.target_value: 2611.13254's open item; 2610.17747's 'residual accuracy' test (scoring judges where cue-only predictors fail) applied to a concrete cue the paper did not name. Who pays: authors reporting Who&When numbers; corpus maintainers.

impact_ceiling.floor: A re-scored table for the methods with released predictions, cited as a footnote to the corpus. Judgment p 0.6.
impact_ceiling.middle: Who&When maintainers publish a clean-split accuracy as the headline metric; one method paper re-reports. Judgment p 0.25.
impact_ceiling.ceiling: The last-speaker artefact is shown to be learned by fine-tuned attribution models (a cue-following test in 2610.17747's sense), changing how attribution judges are trained. Requires a trained method's release. Judgment p 0.1.

scorecard.relevance: Narasimhan route: zero. HAL route: zero. Evaluators and benchmark-validity: direct. Industry: low. Jacob's edge: zero.
scorecard.kill_probe: Steps 0-1: $0, 3 days; dead if no released method moves by more than 2 points and the last-speaker baseline is flat across splits.
scorecard.density_and_ownership: 2610.17747 owns the cue-audit framework ('four tests to separate checking from cue use') and found 'simple predictors match or beat GPT-4.1' on three benchmarks; this probe supplies one named cue on one named split. 2611.13254 owns the split. Methods that would be re-scored: 2608.18575 AFANet and the Who&When paper's baselines (releases to be checked at step 0). Role words: residual accuracy, cue following, label predictability, recency, surface cue, held-out split.

scorecard.register_and_not: A re-analysis of published numbers on a released corpus. It is not a new attribution method and not an annotation study.

title: The conversation the model saw: an offline isloss audit of tau-bench's litellm request stream per provider

glossary.litellm: an open-source Python layer that accepts OpenAI-format chat requests and rewrites them into each provider's API dialect (Anthropic, Google, Bedrock, ...), returning a normalised reply
glossary.isloss / ConvIR: the deterministic oracle of 2611.15543 that maps a source request and its translation to a shared intermediate representation and flags information the target API could have preserved but the translation dropped or changed (avoidable loss), as distinct from loss the target cannot represent
glossary.tool-bearing request: a request whose message list contains at least one tool call and tool result (OpenAI 'role: tool' messages with tool_call_id)
glossary.Tool-Calling scaffold: HAL's tau-bench agent, which is tau-bench's own ToolCallingAgent: one litellm completion per step with the task's tools and temperature 0

statement: Rebuild the message lists tau-bench's ToolCallingAgent sends at every step of a stored airline episode (from HAL's archived records or from fresh runs of one open model), and pass each list, with the airline tool schema, through litellm's offline provider transformations for Anthropic, Google and Bedrock to obtain the provider-bound request without any network call; run isloss on each (source, translated) pair and record $\ell_r \in \{0, 1\}$ (avoidable loss) and its category (role, tool interaction, error state, generation control). Report per provider $p$ the loss share $L_p = \frac{1}{R_p}\sum_r \ell_r$ over all requests and over tool-bearing requests, the category mix, and the share of episodes with at least one lossy request; do the same for the reply path (the normalised reply litellm hands back, including the harness's own truncation to one tool call). Zero model calls.
claim: On tau-bench as HAL ships it, a non-OpenAI model is graded on a conversation litellm rewrote, and for at least one major provider more than one in ten tool-bearing requests loses role or tool information the target API could have kept.
trick: Run the shipped harness's request builder with the network unplugged, diff what it would have sent to each provider against what it meant to send, and count the diffs the provider could have avoided.
why_now: 2611.15543 (2026-11-11) ships a deterministic oracle for exactly this diff ('isloss requires neither a reference translation nor additional model calls') and measured 18.5% avoidable loss on a synthetic suite across five translator codebases; tau-bench's agent and user both call litellm.completion with custom_llm_provider (source fetched 2026-11-15), so the shipped leaderboard harness is a translator in the oracle's sense.

killing_experiment.design: Step 0 ($0, 1 day): read 2611.15543 in full and its released oracle; confirm litellm's provider transformation can be invoked offline for Anthropic, Google and Bedrock at the version HAL pins (read HAL's requirements); confirm a message list can be rebuilt from an archived airline record (the W45 kill report found the user simulator's replies stored per episode). Step 1 ($0, 3 days): rebuild about 50 episodes' request streams (about 500-1,000 requests), translate offline, run isloss, compute $L_p$ by request type and category; repeat on the reply path. Total $0, 0 GPU-h, 4 days.
killing_experiment.kills_if: $L_p < 0.03$ on tool-bearing requests for every provider (Wilson upper bound under 0.05) and no category other than generation controls appears: litellm's translation of this harness's request shape is clean, the claim's mechanism is absent on the shipped benchmark, and C-W46-04 is not run. Also dead at step 0 if the pinned litellm version cannot be driven offline (then the probe needs a recording proxy and is costed again).

preregistered_surprise.expected: Judgment probability 0.6 that $L_p \geq 0.10$ on tool-bearing requests for at least one of Anthropic and Google, dominated by tool-interaction and role categories (the harness's OpenAI-dialect tool messages carry fields the target dialect has no slot for); 0.3 that an error-state category appears (tool errors returned as plain content).
preregistered_surprise.field_assumes: HAL 2602.16666 sec. 7 (quoted in the W45 kill report of CL-W45-01, fetched 2026-11-08): 'We evaluate each benchmark with a single well-performing scaffold'; sec. 4: 'For tau-bench, we use a tool-calling scaffold'. The field reads 'same scaffold' as 'same conversation'. 2611.15543 (abstract): 'a translated request can be accepted by the target API while silently losing information about instruction roles, tool interactions, error states, or generation controls'.
preregistered_surprise.belief_changing: If $L_p \geq 0.10$, a cross-provider leaderboard's 'same scaffold' sends different conversations to different providers and the score-consequence arm (C-W46-04) is owed; if $L_p < 0.03$, the most-used multi-provider harness gets a clean certificate and the lane stops asking.

scorecard.target_value: In print: 2611.15543 ('These results establish conversation preservation as a distinct correctness requirement for ... agent execution, and model evaluation'); 2605.23950's call to disclose the harness; UniACE 2605.27898 ('a reported score reflects a complete model--harness--environment configuration ... tool protocols'). Who pays: HAL, Vals, Artificial Analysis and every leaderboard that routes several providers through one translator; tau-bench and tau2-bench owners; litellm's maintainers.

impact_ceiling.floor: A per-provider loss table for the shipped tau-bench harness, cited by isloss v2 and by HAL's protocol section. Judgment p 0.6.
impact_ceiling.middle: HAL or the tau-bench owners add a translation-audit step (or native-SDK arms) to the protocol; one leaderboard discloses the translator version per row. Requires C-W46-04 to show a score effect. Judgment p 0.25.
impact_ceiling.ceiling: Conversation-preservation certificates become a standard column of cross-provider leaderboards, and the translation path is treated as part of the scaffold in every harness disclosure. Judgment p 0.1.

scorecard.relevance: Narasimhan route (tau-family): direct — the harness is tau-bench's own. HAL route: direct — the protocol column. Evaluators: direct. Industry: direct for anyone running cross-provider evaluations through a gateway. Jacob's edge: software systems moderate; numerics and physics zero.

scorecard.density_and_ownership: Occupant of the oracle and the synthetic-suite number: 2611.15543 (18.5% avoidable loss; 'translation-induced changes can alter model behaviour when tasks depend on the affected information' across six models). Density of the translation-layer conjunction (LiteLLM / API translation / compatibility layer / gateway AND agent AND benchmark/evaluation): 33 total, 0 on a shipped leaderboard harness (fetched 2026-11-15). Role words for the kill search: translation, compatibility layer, gateway, provider dialect, request normalisation, tool_result, role mapping, OpenAI-compatible, ConvIR, SDK parity, harness disclosure, drift.

scorecard.register_and_not: Harness-validity measurement with a protocol consequence. It is not a new translator, not a litellm bug report, and not a claim that any provider is disadvantaged until C-W46-04 runs.

title: Native SDK versus litellm: the same model, the same tasks, two request paths on tau-bench airline

glossary.native SDK arm: the provider's own client library building the request in the provider's dialect from the harness's canonical message list, with a hand-written adapter that preserves every field isloss says is preservable
glossary.replicate floor: the spread between repeated runs of one arm with every setting fixed, measured here from $k = 5$ runs per task within each arm
glossary.pass^k: the chance that all $k$ runs of a task pass

statement: For one provider whose C-W46-03 loss share is highest, run tau-bench airline (50 tasks) with the same model alias, temperature 0, the user simulator pinned to one model at temperature 0 in both arms, $k = 5$ runs per task per arm, one launch window, under (i) the shipped litellm path and (ii) a native-SDK adapter verified lossless by isloss on every request. Readouts: $\Delta = \frac{1}{T}\sum_t (\hat p_t^{\mathrm{nat}} - \hat p_t^{\mathrm{lit}})$ with $\hat p_t^{a} = \frac{1}{k}\sum_{r} Y_{tr}^{a}$ the per-task pass rate in arm $a$ and $Y \in \{0, 1\}$ the tau-bench reward, a task-level paired bootstrap interval on $\Delta$, the same for pass^5, and the within-arm split-half replicate floor; also the per-task count of lossy requests from isloss as a covariate, so that $\Delta$ can be read on lossy against clean tasks.
claim: The same model scores differently on tau-bench airline through litellm than through its native SDK, by more than the five-run replicate interval, and the difference concentrates on the tasks whose requests isloss flagged.
trick: Send the model the conversation it was meant to see, and compare with what the shipped harness sends; if the gap is bigger than the model's own run-to-run wobble, the leaderboard was partly scoring the translator.
why_now: Runs only if C-W46-03 finds $L_p \geq 0.10$; the isloss oracle makes the native arm's losslessness checkable request by request, which no earlier two-path comparison could certify.

killing_experiment.design: Step 0 ($0, 1 day): write the native adapter for the chosen provider; certify it with isloss on the C-W46-03 request stream (zero avoidable loss required). Step 1 (about $300 of API calls for a Sonnet-class model and the pinned user simulator, 0 GPU-h, 4 days): 50 tasks x 2 arms x 5 runs = 500 episodes in one launch window; compute $\Delta$, pass^5 difference, the replicate floor, and the lossy-vs-clean task split. Step 2 (optional, same cost): the second provider. Total: about $300, 0 GPU-h, 5 days.
killing_experiment.kills_if: The paired bootstrap interval on $\Delta$ lies inside the within-arm replicate floor and the pass^5 difference does too, with no excess on isloss-flagged tasks: the translation loss C-W46-03 found does not move the score on this benchmark; the claim is dead as a score claim and survives only as a disclosure note.

preregistered_surprise.expected: Judgment probability 0.35 that $|\Delta|$ exceeds the replicate floor (expected floor from hosted temperature-0 flips: about 9% of single-shot outcomes flip between byte-identical runs, 2607.09691, so a 50-task pass@1 floor near 4 points at $k = 5$); 0.5 that the lossy-task subset shows a gap twice the clean-task subset's.
preregistered_surprise.field_assumes: HAL 2602.16666 sec. 4: temperature 0 'so that any observed variance is attributable to non-sampling sources of stochasticity' — the request path is not among the named sources; 'We evaluate each benchmark with a single well-performing scaffold' (sec. 7).
preregistered_surprise.belief_changing: If the gap exceeds the floor, cross-provider leaderboard rows are not comparable without the translator version and native-SDK arms become the rule; if it does not, translation loss is a documentation matter and the shipped harness is certified for this provider.

scorecard.target_value: As C-W46-03; the score consequence is what HAL's protocol section and the owners' README would act on.

impact_ceiling.floor: A two-arm table for one provider with the replicate floor, cited by HAL and isloss. Judgment p 0.55.
impact_ceiling.middle: Native-SDK arms or a certified translator adopted by one leaderboard. Judgment p 0.25.
impact_ceiling.ceiling: Translator identity treated as part of the scaffold across leaderboards, with a certificate column. Judgment p 0.1.

title: Seeding the world and not the agent: does the policy-draw share near 0.9 hold outside CAGE 4?

glossary.policy sampling seed: the random-number state that decides which action a stochastic policy samples at each step; distinct from the environment seed that fixes the scenario
glossary.policy-draw share: $\hat\rho = \hat\sigma_w^2 / (\hat\sigma_w^2 + \hat\sigma_b^2)$, the within-episode (policy seed) variance over the total in a one-way random-effects decomposition of per-episode returns by environment seed
glossary.learned-defender benchmark: a cyber-defence or similar sequential-decision benchmark whose leaderboard entries are trained policies evaluated against scripted adversaries

statement: For each released learned-agent benchmark with a public evaluation script and at least one released checkpoint (CAGE 2 via CybORG++/MiniCAGE, CAGE 4 as the card, Cyberwheel, and any other the kill search names), record from the script whether the environment and the policy sampling are seeded, and whether the sampling mode (greedy or sampled) is fixed; where a checkpoint and the evaluator run on CPU, evaluate it with $J = 4$ policy seeds on $I = 100$ environment seeds and compute $\hat\rho_b$ with the card's estimator and a bootstrap over episodes. Report the seeding table and $\hat\rho_b$ per benchmark beside CAGE 4's 0.889.
claim: Learned-agent leaderboards in this family seed the scenario and not the policy, and the policy's own draw is the majority of a score's spread in every benchmark checked, not only CAGE 4.
trick: Open each leaderboard's evaluation script, see whether it seeds the agent's dice, and if it does not, roll them four times to see how much of the score was the dice.
why_now: 2611.14068 (2026-11-10) measured 88.9% on one benchmark and released the instrument; the generalisation is checkable on released code without GPUs.

killing_experiment.design: Step 0 ($0, 2 days): read evaluation scripts of CAGE 2 (CybORG++), Cyberwheel and CAGE 4; seeding table. Step 1 ($0, CPU days, 5 days): run released checkpoints under $J = 4$ x $I = 100$; compute $\hat\rho_b$. Total $0, 0 GPU-h, 7 days.
killing_experiment.kills_if: Every other benchmark checked either seeds policy sampling (or reports replicates) or gives $\hat\rho_b < 0.5$: CAGE 4's 0.889 is a property of CAGE 4's reward scale and heavy-tailed episodes, the generalisation is false, and the probe is a footnote to the card paper.

preregistered_surprise.expected: Judgment probability 0.5 that no other checked script seeds policy sampling; 0.35 that $\hat\rho_b > 0.5$ on another benchmark's released checkpoint.
preregistered_surprise.field_assumes: The card: 'the evaluation seeds the environment but not policy sampling, so one command run twice on the same seeds returns different scores' (CAGE 4, sec. 5); CybORG++ 2410.16324 catalogues CAGE 2's defects (invalid actions, inconsistent reward, reduced observation visibility) without a sampling-share measurement (card neighbour).
preregistered_surprise.belief_changing: If the share is high elsewhere, the cyber-RL leaderboards' 'scenario difficulty' reading of score spread is wrong across the family; if not, CAGE 4 is the outlier and its 88.9% is a scale artefact.

scorecard.target_value: 2611.14068's disclosure checklist and its sentence that the four entries above KEEP 'released nothing'; the cyber-RL leaderboard owners. Who pays: CAGE/Cyberwheel maintainers and entrants.

impact_ceiling.floor: A seeding table and two or three $\hat\rho_b$ values beside the card's; a footnote to 2611.14068. Judgment p 0.6.
impact_ceiling.middle: One leaderboard adds policy seeding and a replicate rule. Judgment p 0.2.
impact_ceiling.ceiling: None beyond the cyber-RL family; the LLM-agent version of this sentence is already in print (ICC 2512.06710; HAL's single-run admission; the CL-W43-14 kill record). Judgment p 0.05.

scorecard.relevance: Narasimhan route: zero. HAL route: zero. Evaluators: indirect (a different community). Industry: low. Jacob's edge: variance decompositions and seeds, moderate. Flag: the register is the cyber-RL community's, outside L1's routes.
scorecard.kill_probe: Steps 0-1: $0, 7 days; dead if every other benchmark seeds the policy or gives $\hat\rho_b < 0.5$.
scorecard.density_and_ownership: The card owns the instrument and the CAGE 4 number and recommends the disclosure; CybORG++ owns the CAGE 2 defect catalogue; Trident 2608.04317 is 'the only table stating a run-to-run spread' (card). The generalisation sentence is the card's checklist applied, which is the Gate 2B risk: the card's authors say the leaderboard 'does not say' whether the leading entries carry sampling noise like KEEP's — the expected finding is their stated conditional. Role words: policy seed, evaluation seed, sampling mode, greedy, deterministic evaluation, reproduction interval, replicate, leaderboard protocol.
scorecard.register_and_not: A code audit plus a CPU re-evaluation in another community's register. It is not an L1-route result and not a new defender.

positioning_note: Solo: public code and checkpoints, CPU only.

verdict_by_position.solo: not yet kill-searched; Gate 2B risk stated

neighbors_checked: 2611.14068 — the card: 88.9% policy-draw share on CAGE 4; evaluation seeds the environment only; checklist (full text)
2410.16324 CybORG++ — CAGE 2 reimplementation with a defect catalogue; no sampling share (card neighbour)
2608.04317 Trident — the only audited table stating a run-to-run spread (card neighbour)
2610.00557 — cross-environment red teams on CAGE 4 and Cyberwheel; omits dispersion and seeds (card neighbour)
headline_test: If the share is high elsewhere: learned-defender leaderboards across the family report one roll of the agent's dice as the agent's skill.

history.note: mutate W46 from 2611.14068, operators 5 (the cross-benchmark comparison the audit did not run) and 4 (the share as a ruler on other leaderboards); filed as an orphan sketch with a stated Gate 2B risk — the card's authors state the generalisation as a conditional, and the LLM-agent version is already in print; weakest of the five

title: The return is an operating point: the orchestrator's error against the return rate (final answer / 80-token evidence block / 200-token summary / full trace) on frozen executor traces, with the orchestrator's accept-or-re-delegate decision as the relevant variable

glossary.orchestrator / executor: in 2611.16526 the orchestrator is the model instance that holds the user's question, writes one brief per fact and integrates the answers; the executor is a fresh instance of the same model with the web tools that answers one brief and returns text
glossary.brief: the message the orchestrator writes down to the executor (the rewritten sub-question)
glossary.return: the message the executor writes up to the orchestrator; in the paper only its final answer ('neither the executor's intermediate trajectory nor the contents returned by its web tools', App. A)
glossary.return rate: the length in tokens of the return message; 'rate' in the rate-distortion sense (bits spent on the description)
glossary.frozen trace: an executor run stored once (queries, snippets, opened pages, HTTP failures, final answer) and replayed to the orchestrator byte-identical in every arm, so tool budget, page content and failures cannot differ across arms
glossary.knee: the smallest return rate at which the orchestrator recovers a pre-set fraction (0.8) of the accuracy gap between answer-only and full-trace returns
glossary.decoder side information: information the receiver already holds and uses to decode a message; here the orchestrator's closed-book answer, right before the model's training cutoff and wrong after it
glossary.post-cutoff: facts dated after the model's training data ends, so the model's memory of them is wrong by construction (closed-book accuracy 0.00-0.06 in the paper's Table 2)
glossary.matched loss: the single agent's accuracy minus the delegated system's accuracy when both have the same pooled tool budget and the same tool-use instruction
glossary.two-player Shapley split: the unique split of a loss between two causes (brief, return) that averages each cause's marginal effect over both orders of inclusion; efficient (the shares sum to the loss), symmetric, a dummy gets zero
glossary.delivered and ignored: evidence that was in the receiving agent's input and was not used (2611.13254's category: 'in an agent's input and was never mentioned')

statement: Rebuild the forced-delegation arm of 2611.16526 on the two datasets whose ground truth is a public API (GDP: World Bank NY.GDP.MKTP.KD.ZG, 30 four-country sets for 2019 and 2025; Nobel: Nobel Prize API, laureates 2014-2019 and 2025-2026; about 72 prompts and 310 items per split pair) with gpt-oss-120b as orchestrator and executor on vLLM at the paper's temperature 1.0, GPT-5 as the API arm (the paper's largest-loss model) and Qwen3-30B-A3B-Thinking-2507 as a sign-check arm (it gains under forced delegation in 6 of 8 cells, Table 2); freeze the orchestrator's briefs $u_i$ and each executor trace $C_i$ (queries, snippets, opened pages, HTTP failures, final answer $a_i$) over a day-1 web cache shared with C-W46-08, then replay the orchestrator's integration step on the same bytes at four return rates: $M^{(0)}_i = a_i$ (the paper's setting), $M^{(1)}_i = (a_i, \text{source URL}, \text{quoted snippet} \le 25 \text{ words}, \text{tool-failure list})$ at most 80 tokens by deterministic extraction, $M^{(2)}_i$ the executor's own 200-token summary written once and frozen, $M^{(3)}_i = C_i$ the full trace, plus a fifth arm using the paper's own executor-written 'report inaccessible URLs' field so the knee is not one schema's artifact. Read, against API ground truth $y^\star_i$ and never from a judge: the item error $D(R) = \Pr[\hat y^{(R)}_i \ne y^\star_i]$, the gap $G = D(R_0) - D(R_3)$, the recovered fraction $\phi(R) = [D(R_0) - D(R)] / G$, the knee $R^\star = \min\{R : \phi(R) \ge 0.8\}$ in tokens, the decision error $D_Z(R)$ (accept / re-delegate / override, read from whether call_subagent was issued again and whether the final answer equals $a_i$, against the oracle rule accept iff $a_i = y^\star_i$), items split by whether $a_i$ equals the orchestrator's closed-book answer $b_i$ from the no-tool arm, the delivered-and-ignored share $D(R_3 \mid C_i \text{ holds } y^\star_i)$ (the handoff version of 2611.13254's 'in an agent's input and never mentioned'), and tokens per arm; $n = 3$ orchestrator draws at temperature 1.0 and one at temperature 0, prompt-cluster bootstrap.
claim: On fact lookups the executor-to-orchestrator return is an operating point on a curve with a knee under 80 tokens: a structured evidence block recovers at least 0.8 of the answer-only-to-full-trace accuracy gap, so 'full traces would undermine the context-saving benefits' names a trade-off that a 50-token schema settles.
trick: Store each subagent's run once, hand the boss the same run four times at four lengths, and see how short the note can be before the boss starts making the same mistakes as with the bare answer.
why_now: 2611.16526 (2026-11-12) measured the answer-only return's cost in accuracy on datasets whose ground truth is a public API, so a frozen-trace replay is a one-week build; 2607.16133 (2026-07-17) wrote the relay bottleneck for worker-to-worker messages and left the aggregator's input uncompressed with the relay complexity assigned by hand; 2611.17041 (2026-11-12) and 2606.09730 (2026-06) made the subagent report a training target with a rubric and no schema; 2610.15938 (2026-10-11) ran the shown-rate design for a judge ('about a tenth of the source did almost all' of the work) and nobody has run it for an orchestrator.

killing_experiment.design: Step 1 (3 days, no GPU): rebuild the GDP and Nobel prompt sets from the APIs following 2611.16526 sec. 3 and Table 6; write the three-stage harness (freeze briefs; run executors and store traces; replay returns) and the four return formatters, sharing the web cache and harness with C-W46-08. Step 2 (about 6 GPU-hours on 1 H100 with vLLM, 1 day, about $75 of SerpAPI): for gpt-oss-120b and Qwen3-30B-A3B run the closed-book arm (for $b_i$), the brief stage, two executor traces per item under orchestrator-written briefs and one under verbatim-item briefs, about 1,000 executor runs; record the executor hit share $E = \Pr[a_i = y^\star_i]$ and the share of traces that hold $y^\star_i$ anywhere. Step 3 (about 4 GPU-hours, 1 day): orchestrator integration on the frozen traces at the five rates, $n = 3$ draws at temperature 1.0 and one at temperature 0, about 2,500 short runs. Step 4 (2 days): $D(R)$, $D_Z(R)$, $\phi(R)$, $R^\star$, the side-information split, the delivered-and-ignored share, tokens per arm, prompt-cluster bootstrap. Step 5 (about $300 API, 1 day): the same replay on GPT-5, the headline's second model; promoted from optional to required because the open models' losses in the paper are small or of the wrong sign.
killing_experiment.dollars: about $40 of H100 spot plus about $75 of SerpAPI calls; about $300 more for the GPT-5 arm; about $415 in all
killing_experiment.days: 8 days: 3 of harness and data work, 2 of runs, 2 of analysis, 1 for the GPT-5 arm
killing_experiment.kills_if: Dead as a probe of CL-W46-03 if $\phi(R_1) < 0.4$ on both headline models (gpt-oss-120b, GPT-5) under both $R_1$ schemas with the bootstrap interval's upper end under 0.6 (the curve is gradual; no compact decision-sufficient statistic exists for this shape; the context-saving conflict stands), or if $G = D(R_0) - D(R_3) < 2$ pp on both headline models with traces frozen (the return channel is not where the loss went; the result is a confound note on 2611.16526). Dead as a ruler if fewer than 80% of post-cutoff items have closed-book accuracy under 0.06 on a model (the split is not post-cutoff for it), if the temperature-1.0 and temperature-0 knees differ by more than one rate level on both models (the knee is a sampling artifact), or if the frozen traces hold $y^\star_i$ for under 60% of post-cutoff items on both models (the executor, not the return, is where the items are lost, and the curve has nothing to recover).

preregistered_surprise.expected: Judgment, not evidence: probability 0.35 that $\phi(R_1) \ge 0.8$ on both headline models (knee at or under 80 tokens); 0.30 that $\phi(R_1) \in [0.4, 0.8)$ (knee at the 200-token summary or no knee below the full trace); 0.35 that $\phi(R_1) < 0.4$ on at least one model. The paper's own one-field variant (report inaccessible URLs: GPT-5 GDP post-cutoff $0.43 \to 0.51$ against a single-agent 0.89; GPT-OSS $0.70 \to 0.62$, sec. 6) recovered under a fifth of its gap with budgets and briefs unmatched, which is why the knee is not given more than 0.35. Probability 0.5 that at $R_0$ the error on items with $a_i \ne b_i$ exceeds the error on $a_i = b_i$ items by at least 10 pp and that the excess falls under 3 pp at $R_1$.
preregistered_surprise.field_assumes: 2611.16526 sec. 7: 'Passing complete executor traces to the orchestrator could mitigate the loss of information, but would undermine the context-saving benefits of delegation'; sec. 6: 'Addressing this challenge may require targeted mechanisms for communicating evidence and resolving conflicts rather than simple prompt interventions'. 2607.16133 sec. 3 (full text read by the import, 2026-11-15): 'The system-level aggregator then combines all terminal memories into the final output'; sec. 7: relay complexity is 'assigned by task-structure analysis rather than estimating it quantitatively'. 2604.02460 abstract (fetched 2026-11-15): 'under a fixed reasoning-token budget and with perfect context utilization, single-agent systems are more information-efficient'. 2611.13254 sec. 4.2 (card): in failed multi-agent runs the contradicting evidence 'was in an agent's input and was never mentioned' in 41 of 68 runs, so the loss between agents is attention, not transmission.
preregistered_surprise.belief_changing: If the knee is at or under 80 tokens, the 'delegation boundary' cost on fact lookups is an operating-point choice worth about 10 points and 50-80 tokens, every harness that returns final answers has a schema to ship, MAS-versus-SAS papers report the return rate they operated at, and 2607.16133's relay complexity has an estimator for this channel. If $\phi(R_1) < 0.4$, the orchestrator's decision depends on diffuse trace content and the recipe is not to isolate contexts for lookups the orchestrator must adjudicate. If $G < 2$ pp with traces frozen, the paper's 10-point loss did not pass through the return (budget, instruction and brief confounds), which revises the card. If the delivered-and-ignored share at $R_3$ exceeds $G$, 2611.13254's reading (attention, not transmission) holds for this handoff too.

identifiability: Random given: fixed prompt set, frozen briefs and executor traces (every rate arm replays the same bytes, so tool budgets, page contents and HTTP failures are identical across arms by construction), fixed orchestrator model and prompt with only the return field changed, deterministic $R_1$ extraction (URL and snippet copied from the opened page that contains the answer string; failures copied from HTTP status). Whose temperature: the orchestrator's integration step at 1.0 as in the paper, with $n = 3$ draws and a temperature-0 arm; $D(R)$ is an error rate, defined at any temperature, not a variance. Whose property: the curve belongs to (orchestrator model, prompt, schema) on this item population; the executor is frozen. Post-cutoff status checked per model by the closed-book arm (under 0.06 as in Table 2); Qwen's cutoff is a release date and 'may therefore be earlier' (App. A). Verifier, not judge: exact match against the World Bank and Nobel APIs (GDP within 0.1 points as in the paper); the decision $Z$ is read from tool calls.

scorecard.target_value: In print: 2611.16526 sec. 7 (the trade-off sentence) and sec. 6 ('targeted mechanisms for communicating evidence'); 2607.16133 sec. 7 ('Future work should develop quantitative estimators for both'); 2611.17041 abstract (fetched): 'subagents must return reliable evidence', a rubric on 'the research utility of each subagent report'; 2606.09730 abstract (fetched): 'constraining subagents to return results'; 2611.13254 sec. 4.2. Who pays: every harness that returns final answers from subagents (Claude Code subagents, OpenAI Agents SDK handoffs, Magentic-One's ledger); delegation-training teams whose rubric grades the return; MAS-versus-SAS authors whose comparisons sit at an unreported rate.

impact_ceiling.floor: gradual curve or $G < 2$ pp: a footnote that the return channel for fact lookups is high-complexity or that Lost in Delegation's loss did not pass through it; cited by 2607.16133's successors and the paper's authors. Requires steps 1-4. Judgment p 0.35.
impact_ceiling.middle: knee at or under 80 tokens on both headline models with the post-cutoff excess closing at $R_1$: a measurement with a schema consequence any orchestrator harness can adopt and a quantitative relay complexity for one channel; proper idea, one community (harness builders) changes a default. Requires steps 1-5 and both $R_1$ schemas. Judgment p 0.40.
impact_ceiling.ceiling: the same knee shape on a second task family with execution-based scoring (a SWE-style subagent return or ClawArena-Team), so 'return rate operated at' becomes a reported column in MAS-versus-SAS papers and the structured return a default in two public harnesses. Requires about 20 more GPU-hours. Judgment p 0.25.

scorecard.relevance: L4 all routes (a handoff measured for what it costs in tokens and accuracy, with a schema consequence); Narasimhan route through the MAS-versus-SAS measurement register; HAL and evaluators through L1 (frozen traces remove the budget and prompt confounds); product teams directly. L2 at the margin (LEAD-RL's rubric is the training consumer); L3 only as tokens saved per return; L5 zero. Jacob's edge: direct, rate-distortion, sufficiency and the information bottleneck are his to check and say in a talk; the design has no learned component.
scorecard.kill_probe: Steps 1-5: frozen traces on rebuilt GDP and Nobel sets, five return rates, gpt-oss-120b and GPT-5 (Qwen as sign check); about 12 GPU-hours and $415; 8 days; dead if $\phi(R_1) < 0.4$ on both headline models under both schemas (interval upper end under 0.6) or $G < 2$ pp on both.
scorecard.density_and_ownership: Occupied: the information-bottleneck objective for inter-agent relays (2607.16133; 2606.13733's min-cut bound; 2604.02460's data-processing argument; GoAgent 2603.19677 as a method; IMAC 1911.06992 and CGIBNet 2112.10374 in MARL); the single-point measurement of the answer-only return (2611.16526); the shown-rate design for a judge (2610.15938, fetched 2026-11-15: 'what the judge was shown mattered more than which judge it was'; 'About a tenth of the source did almost all'); harness pressure on 'return results properly' (SearchSwarm 2606.09730; MS-Eval 2610.22869's MAD-SAE benchmark with isolated contexts); return rubrics in training (LEAD-RL 2611.17041). Unoccupied in every fetched source: a rate sweep of the executor-to-orchestrator return on frozen traces, the orchestrator's decision as the relevant variable, the knee as an estimated relay complexity, the orchestrator's prior as decoder side information, tokens counted per return. First movers: the 2611.16526 authors (datasets; release unknown), the TAMU group (formalism), SearchSwarm / LEAD-RL (trained delegators); the re-open test is asking them. Density counted 2026-11-15: the import's 13 field-word and 82 lane-word hits; this run's return-format query 15 hits all time, 3 since 2026-10-16 (about one a month). Race window about three months against an 8-day probe.
scorecard.why_now: 2607.16133 (2026-07-17); 2611.16526 (2026-11-12) with public-API ground truth; 2611.17041 and 2606.09730 as training consumers with a rubric and no schema; 2610.15938 (2026-10-11) as the shown-rate design in another role; the two open models serve on one H100 under vLLM.
scorecard.register_and_not: Measurement: a distortion-rate curve at five operating points on frozen traces, with a mechanism (the orchestrator decides with a few bits the bare answer discards; its prior is a wrong decoder post-cutoff) and a consequence each way. It is not a new orchestrator, not a relay-training method, not a bound, not a compaction result (the W42 S3xF5 record was closed), and not a re-analysis of 2611.16526's judge-labelled return reactions.

positioning_note: Solo: public APIs, two open models on one H100, about $415. Lab (a harness team or the paper's authors): the same replay on owned traces before shipping a return schema.

title: Who lost the item: randomised replacement of the brief and the return at the single agent's tool budget and instruction, with the two-player Shapley split of the matched delegation loss and the share of lost items with no single responsible message

glossary.orchestrator / executor: in 2611.16526 the orchestrator is the model instance that holds the user's question, writes one brief per fact and integrates the answers; the executor is a fresh instance of the same model with the web tools that answers one brief and returns text
glossary.brief: the message the orchestrator writes down to the executor (the rewritten sub-question)
glossary.return: the message the executor writes up to the orchestrator; in the paper only its final answer ('neither the executor's intermediate trajectory nor the contents returned by its web tools', App. A)
glossary.return rate: the length in tokens of the return message; 'rate' in the rate-distortion sense (bits spent on the description)
glossary.frozen trace: an executor run stored once (queries, snippets, opened pages, HTTP failures, final answer) and replayed to the orchestrator byte-identical in every arm, so tool budget, page content and failures cannot differ across arms
glossary.knee: the smallest return rate at which the orchestrator recovers a pre-set fraction (0.8) of the accuracy gap between answer-only and full-trace returns
glossary.decoder side information: information the receiver already holds and uses to decode a message; here the orchestrator's closed-book answer, right before the model's training cutoff and wrong after it
glossary.post-cutoff: facts dated after the model's training data ends, so the model's memory of them is wrong by construction (closed-book accuracy 0.00-0.06 in the paper's Table 2)
glossary.matched loss: the single agent's accuracy minus the delegated system's accuracy when both have the same pooled tool budget and the same tool-use instruction
glossary.two-player Shapley split: the unique split of a loss between two causes (brief, return) that averages each cause's marginal effect over both orders of inclusion; efficient (the shares sum to the loss), symmetric, a dummy gets zero
glossary.delivered and ignored: evidence that was in the receiving agent's input and was not used (2611.13254's category: 'in an agent's input and was never mentioned')

statement: Rebuild 2611.16526's GDP set (World Bank NY.GDP.MKTP.KD.ZG, the same 30 four-country sets, 2019 and 2025, $N = 60$ prompts, $n = 240$ items) and its post-cutoff Books set (Goodreads 2026, $N = 20$, $n = 100$), cache the web on day 1 so every arm sees the same pages, and run gpt-oss-120b on vLLM at temperature 1.0 with $r = 5$ runs per prompt per arm across six arms: $A_0$ single agent at the paper's protocol; $D_u$ forced delegation at the paper's protocol (2 searches and 3 opens per executor, the executor's 'only call a tool if you are not sure' instruction, Tables 7-8); and the matched factorial $D(b, r)$, $b, r \in \{0, 1\}$, where $b = 1$ means the orchestrator writes the brief and $b = 0$ the harness passes the user's item verbatim, $r = 1$ means the executor returns only its final answer and $r = 0$ the harness appends C-W46-07's deterministic $R_1$ block (source URL, quoted snippet of at most 25 words, tool-failure list; at most 80 tokens), with the pooled budget $2n$ searches and $3n$ opens shared across executors through a global counter and the single agent's instruction given to every executor. With $p_i(a)$ the item's success rate under arm $a$ and $v(S) = \bar p$ when the lossy channels in $S \subseteq \{B, R\}$ are active: the unmatched loss $\Delta_u = \bar p(A_0) - \bar p(D_u)$, the matched loss $L = \bar p(A_0) - \bar p(D(1,1))$, the cutoff difference-in-differences, the two-player Shapley shares $$\phi_B = \tfrac{1}{2}\big[(v(\emptyset) - v(\{B\})) + (v(\{R\}) - v(\{B,R\}))\big], \qquad \phi_B + \phi_R = v(\emptyset) - v(\{B,R\}),$$ the interaction $I = v(\{B,R\}) - v(\{B\}) - v(\{R\}) + v(\emptyset)$, the residual $\bar p(A_0) - v(\emptyset)$ (the cost of separate contexts with both messages lossless), the headline cell $\rho_{80} = [v(\{B\}) - v(\{B,R\})] / L$ (what the 80-token return recovers of the matched loss with the brief still orchestrator-written), and for lost items (correct under $A_0$ in at least 4 of 5 runs, wrong under $D(1,1)$ in at least 4 of 5) the share whose outcome flips under exactly one channel swap. Step 2 repeats the six arms on GPT-5 for GDP; step 3 adds the full-trace return arm with tokens counted so the paper's 'extreme' sits on the same ruler.
claim: With tool budget and executor instruction matched, the post-cutoff delegation loss of 2611.16526 is at most half the reported one, and of what remains the return channel carries at least half: appending an 80-token evidence block to the bare answer recovers at least half of the matched loss, while a verbatim brief alone does not.
trick: Run the delegated system four times with each of the two messages either as the model writes it or replaced by a harness-made lossless version, at the same search budget as the lone agent, and read off which message loses the points by subtraction.
why_now: 2611.16526 (2026-11-12) published the grid with arms unmatched in budget (Table 7) and instruction (Table 8) and four judged rates as attribution ('may contribute to the observed lower accuracy', sec. 5.3); 2611.13254 (2026-11-09) wrote that control reach and responsible-agent labels are trace readings, 'not a measured intervention'; 2608.04893 (2026-08) established the randomised-replacement audit of a MAS channel with pre-registered equivalence margins, so the probe is a harness with a budget counter and two switches.

killing_experiment.design: Step 1 (about 25 GPU-hours on 2 H100, 7 days including 4 of harness work shared with C-W46-07, about $350 of SerpAPI): rebuild the sets; harness with a global budget counter, a verbatim-brief switch, the deterministic $R_1$ return block and a day-1 web cache; 80 prompts x 6 arms x 5 runs = 2,400 prompt-runs on gpt-oss-120b; compute $\Delta_u$, $L$, DiD, $\phi_B$, $\phi_R$, $I$, the residual, $\rho_{80}$, the lost-item flip table, prompt-bootstrap intervals ($B = 1000$) and the run-to-run component. Step 2 (about $450 API, 2 days): the six arms on GPT-5 for GDP (the paper's largest loss cell, $0.89 \to 0.35$). Step 3 (about 5 GPU-hours, 1 day): the full-trace return arm $D(1, \text{trace})$ with tokens counted. Optional step 4 (about $200): pre-cutoff GDP on GPT-5 for the matched DiD.
killing_experiment.dollars: about $350 SerpAPI plus about $90 H100 spot for steps 1 and 3; about $450 GPT-5 API for step 2; about $1,100 in all (step 1 alone about $440)
killing_experiment.days: 11 days: 4 of harness and dataset rebuild, 3 of runs, 2 of analysis, 2 for the GPT-5 arm
killing_experiment.kills_if: Dead for CL-W46-03's headline if $\rho_{80} < 0.4$ on both gpt-oss-120b and GPT-5 with the prompt-bootstrap interval's upper end under 0.6 (the 80-token return does not recover half the matched loss). Dead as an import if, on the post-cutoff sets, both channel swaps move item accuracy by under 2 points with intervals covering zero and $L$ is within 2 points of $\Delta_u$ (the loss sits in context separation itself; the messages-as-players framing has nothing to credit). Premise void (recorded, not a kill of the design) if $L < 2$ pp on both models: the headline's loss is a budget-and-instruction artifact and the result is the protocol footnote. Parked if per-cell interval half-widths exceed 5 points at $r = 5$ (re-open with the full 120-prompt Books set). Dead as a testbed if the rebuilt single-agent GDP accuracy misses the paper's gpt-oss-120b cell (0.92 pre-cutoff) by more than 10 points.

preregistered_surprise.expected: Judgment, not evidence: probability 0.5 that $L \le \Delta_u / 2$ (matched loss at most half the reported), 0.3 that it lies between half and the full loss, 0.2 that matching changes nothing. For the split of $L$: 0.35 that the return carries at least half ($\rho_{80} \ge 0.5$, the CL-W46-03 headline), 0.45 that the brief carries at least 0.6 (the paper's sec. 5.1 reading with an identified number), 0.2 that the interaction is as large as a main effect. Probability 0.45 that fewer than half of the lost items flip under exactly one swap. The two S10 imports disagree here (F5 expected the return knee, F8 the brief), which is what makes the cell informative: the probe decides a fork, not a confirmation.
preregistered_surprise.field_assumes: 2611.16526 sec. 2: 'we isolate the effect of delegating tool access on performance'; sec. 5.3: the four rates 'may contribute to the observed lower accuracy'; sec. 5.1: 'Query rewriting can alter the task itself'; sec. 7: full traces 'would undermine the context-saving benefits'. 2611.13254 sec. 5.1: '"Would have reached" is a judgment about the trace ... It is not a measured intervention'. The attribution line (Who&When 2505.00212, card neighbour) assumes a 'responsible agent' and 'decisive step' exist per failed run and are readable from the trace.
preregistered_surprise.belief_changing: If $L \le 2$ points post-cutoff, the 9-11 point headline is a budget-and-instruction artifact and every same-model orchestration comparison must match the pooled tool budget and the executor instruction before claiming a boundary effect. If the return carries at least half, the brief-distortion account is a symptom and the return schema is the recipe, with its fields priced per token. If the interaction is as large as a main effect or fewer than half of lost items flip under one swap, no single message is responsible for most lost items on a testbed where every counterfactual was run, so a single 'responsible agent' label is unidentified by construction and attribution benchmarks need an intervention-identified label beside the human one. If the brief carries at least 0.6 and $L \approx \Delta_u$, the paper's reading stands with an identified number and a verbatim-brief recipe: a footnote.

identifiability: Random given: fixed item text, model and weights, sampling (temperature 1.0, top-p 1.0 as in App. A), the cached web (so arm order and run date are not confounded with search results). Assignment: each (prompt, run) is assigned to an arm by the harness at random, so exchangeability holds by construction and arm contrasts are average causal effects of the protocol on item correctness; $b$ and $r$ are assigned independently, so each main effect and the interaction is identified. Whose temperature: both parties at 1.0; the quantities are mean contrasts, defined at temperature 0 as well (a party at temperature 0 has zero decision variance and a nonzero contrast); the run-to-run component is reported beside them. Whose property: $\phi_B$, $\phi_R$, $I$ and $\rho_{80}$ belong to the (model, harness protocol, schema) triple and are reported per model, never as 'the model's'. Caveat: the verbatim-brief arm removes the decomposition step too, which is trivial on GDP and Books (items are listed in the user prompt) and would not be on interdependent tasks. Verifier, not judge: exact numeric (GDP within 0.1 points) or exact title match (Books); the paper's four judged rates are not used.

scorecard.target_value: In print: 2611.16526 sec. 5.3, 6 and 7 (quoted above; tokens never counted); 2611.13254 sec. 5.1 (not a measured intervention; 45% of a public attribution split scored on harness-generated answers attributed to agents); 2604.02460's equal-compute premise. Who pays: every team deploying orchestrator-subagent systems and choosing a return schema or brief rewriting; MAS-versus-SAS authors; owners of attribution benchmarks whose labels are trained on.

impact_ceiling.floor: matched loss near the unmatched loss and the brief carrying most of it: the paper's sec. 5.1 reading confirmed with an identified number, a verbatim-brief recipe and a matched-protocol replication. Requires step 1. Judgment p 0.35.
impact_ceiling.middle: matched loss at most half the headline or one channel's share at least 0.6 with intervals, consistent across the two models: orchestration studies match budgets and report per-channel credit, product teams pick return fields by marginal contribution. Requires steps 1-2. Judgment p 0.45.
impact_ceiling.ceiling: no single message responsible for most lost items where every coalition was run, so 'responsible agent' labels are shown unidentified on a controlled testbed and an attribution benchmark adopts an intervention-identified label. Requires steps 1-3 and the flip-table result on both models (about $1,300). Judgment p 0.2.

scorecard.relevance: L4 all routes (the brief and the return measured for what they cost, causally, at matched tokens); L1 directly (attribution of the outcome to who moved, by intervention; HAL and Narasimhan evaluators as consumers of the identifiability result); L2 only as the measurement side of multi-agent credit (SHARP-style Shapley rewards validated, not replaced); L3 and L5 zero. Industry: direct (return schema and brief rewriting are knobs product teams own). Jacob's edge: a $2 \times 2$ factorial, the two-player Shapley identity, a difference-in-differences and an interaction term, checked on a napkin; 'reading a record identifies nothing, randomising does' is his to say in a talk.
scorecard.kill_probe: Step 1: six arms x 80 prompts x 5 runs on gpt-oss-120b with a cached web, about 25 GPU-hours and $440, 7 days; dead for the headline if $\rho_{80} < 0.4$ on both models (upper end under 0.6); dead as an import if both swaps move accuracy under 2 points and $L \approx \Delta_u$.
scorecard.density_and_ownership: The failure-attribution line is dense (the import counted 54 arXiv hits for 'failure attribution' with multi-agent words, about two a week since 2026-05), nearly all trace-reading judges or benchmarks of them (BLADE, Who&When Pro, TraceElephant, MAScope 2610.10126 fetched 2026-11-15: a topology-conditioned judge over traces). Occupied: randomised replacement of a latent KV channel (2608.04893); skip interventions on components as a learner (2609.30734, fetched: 'controlled skip interventions reveal the consequences of omitting a future step'); counterfactual replay as a label factory (AgenTracer 2509.03312, import neighbour); Shapley credit over agents as reward (SHARP 2602.08335, 2511.10687); the unmatched grid with judged rates (2611.16526); per-layer omission attribution (2607.22448). Unoccupied in every fetched source: randomising the brief and the return of a text handoff at matched budget and instruction against a single agent, the Shapley split of a delegation loss between the two messages, the matched cutoff DiD, the share of lost items with no single responsible unit. First movers: the 2611.16526 authors (harness and datasets; release unknown) and the 2608.04893 authors (the audit design); the re-open test is asking them. Race: the paper is three days old; a matched-budget follow-up from its authors inside two to three months is the live threat against an 11-day probe.
scorecard.why_now: 2611.16526 (2026-11-12); 2611.13254 (2026-11-09); 2610.17747 (2026-10-13, import neighbour: attribution judges follow surface cues); 2608.04893 (2026-08, the replacement-audit design); pre/post-cutoff paired datasets (2605.28721, 2611.16526) give a memory-is-wrong condition that makes a folded-in guess detectable.
scorecard.register_and_not: Measurement: a randomised factorial with a two-player Shapley split and a difference-in-differences; a mechanism (a rewritten brief folds a wrong guess into the executor's task; an unmatched instruction converts wrong memory into skipped searches; a bare answer is weighed against a wrong prior); three consequences (match budgets before claiming a boundary effect; price return fields per token; add an intervention-identified attribution label). It is not a new orchestrator, not a trace-reading judge, not an RL credit method, and not a variance split: the quantities are mean contrasts.
