title: A lesson's hazard against its use-age: the paired per-use harm of a self-written lesson by use-age bin, with lesson frailty and store crowding separated and a frozen-store null

glossary.lesson / insight: a short rule an agent writes for itself after a task from that task's success- or failure-labelled trajectory (WikiTrace's 'insight'; FGSE's 'experience-derived behavioral update')
glossary.memory-induced degradation: WikiTrace's term: the agent fails a task it solves with the lesson withheld
glossary.use-age: a lesson's retrieval count $u$: its $u$-th use is its age $u$
glossary.paired per-use harm: $\hat\delta_{\ell u} = (c_{\ell u} - a_{\ell u}) / n$, the success count over $n$ runs with lesson $\ell$ withheld minus the count with it in the retrieved set, on the task where its $u$-th retrieval fell; positive means the lesson hurt
glossary.hazard shape: how the mean harm moves with use-age: falling (defects at birth), flat (a per-use draw), rising (wear-out); reliability engineering's bathtub, with the power law $m(u) = a b\, u^{b-1}$, $b < 1$ falling, $b = 1$ flat, $b > 1$ rising
glossary.frailty: a per-lesson random effect $z_\ell$ (mean 1): some lessons are harmful at every use, most never; a mixture of flat hazards at different levels reads as a falling pooled hazard, which is why frailty is fitted before the shape is read
glossary.crowding: the dependence of a lesson's harm on the size of the store it is retrieved with, $|M_{\ell u}|^{\gamma}$; Library Drift's 'false-positive injections' read at lesson grain
glossary.frozen-store null: the store frozen after pass 1 and passes 2-3 replayed against it, where every use of a lesson is a draw from the same task distribution against the same store, so the hazard is flat by construction
glossary.burn-in / per-use inspection / scheduled: reliability engineering's three maintenance policies: screen units before shipment (FGSE's admission probes), inspect at every use (WikiTrace's descent to the source trajectory), replace at an age or capacity bound (TrackRL's retirement, Library Drift's active cap)

statement: Run WikiTrace's released insights-only store (github.com/yukyeongleee/wikitrace: lessons distilled from labelled trajectories, no evidence links) on ALFWorld's 134 unseen tasks for 3 passes in a seeded order with the actor its code names (Qwen3-30B-A3B or Qwen3.5-9B) under vLLM at the deployed sampling setting read from the code, logging every (lesson, task) retrieval; at each task run the with-arm $n = 4$ times (one shared arm per task, as CoReMem 2611.17316 shares its no-memory arm) and, for each of the about four retrieved lessons, the withhold-one arm $n = 4$ times, giving about 1,500 (lesson, use) pairs and $\hat\delta_{\ell u}$ for each. Read the signed mean harm $\bar\delta(U)$ by use-age bin $U \in \{1\}, \{2,3\}, \{4\text{-}7\}, \{8+\}$ with a lesson-cluster bootstrap (never a binarised 'induced failure' event, whose false rate at $n = 3$ and $q = 0.5$ is 0.25), then the parametric summary $\mathbb{E}[\hat\delta_{\ell u} \mid z_\ell] = z_\ell\, \lambda\, u^{\beta - 1}\, |M_{\ell u}|^{\gamma}$ with $z_\ell$ the lesson frailty (mean 1, variance $\sigma^2$), $\lambda$ the level, $\beta$ the aging shape and $\gamma$ the crowding exponent, fitted with the frailty as a random effect; against a frozen-store arm (store frozen after pass 1, passes 2-3 replayed; $\beta = 1$ by construction) and two more task orders, and with the symmetric benefit $-\hat\delta$ by bin reported so the ruler is two-sided. Then the burn-in leakage: with $p_\ell$ a harmful lesson's per-use harm probability, $k$ admission probes catch it with probability $1 - (1 - p_\ell)^{k}$, and the predicted share of harmful lessons surviving $k = 3, 10, 30$ probes is read against FGSE's 3.6% harmful committed updates.
claim: A lesson's per-use harm is set by the store it is retrieved with, not by its birth or its own age: the mean harm rises by at least 0.05 from a lesson's first to its eighth-or-later use in the growing store and by under 0.03 in the same store frozen, and the rise is absorbed when store size enters the model, so admission probes and per-use inspection are aimed at a defect that is not where the harm comes from and a capacity or age bound is the design that pays.
trick: Treat each self-written lesson like a shipped part, record how much it hurts at its first, third and tenth use with the same store frozen as a control, and let the shape of that curve say whether to test lessons at birth, check them every time, or throw them out at an age.
why_now: WikiTrace (2026-11-10) named memory-induced degradation at lesson grain and released code with an insights-only arm, so per-lesson withholding is a configuration change; FGSE (2026-11-10) published an admission-battery residual (3.6%) that a hazard-and-probe-count formula can predict; TrackRL (2026-10-18) made within-group random withholding the standard per-skill estimator; 2610.17544 (2026-10-13) wrote the constant-within-epoch assumption down; CoReMem (2026-11-12) defined a memory's value as the with/without next-task contrast; 2610.33029 (2026-10-12) measured that lessons carry chance from lucky runs, the frailty-at-birth mechanism.

killing_experiment.design: Step 1 (about 18 GPU-hours, 6 days including 3 of harness work): WikiTrace insights-only on ALFWorld's 134 unseen tasks, 3 passes, seeded order, 9B or 30B-A3B actor under vLLM at the deployed temperature; log retrievals; per task the with-arm x4 and the withhold-one arm x4 per retrieved lesson (about 20 episodes per task, about 8,000 episodes, about 1,500 pairs); bin means with lesson-cluster bootstrap; the frailty / aging / crowding fit, reporting the design's condition number for $(\beta, \gamma)$ since use-age and store size both grow with time and are separated only by lessons born in different passes and by the task orders. Step 2 (about 10 GPU-hours, 2 days): the frozen-store arm and two more task orders. Step 3 (1 day, no compute): burn-in leakage from the fitted $p_\ell$ distribution against FGSE's 3.6%. Optional step 4 (about $400 API or 25 GPU-hours): AppWorld with one API actor, to check the shape is not an ALFWorld fact.
killing_experiment.dollars: about $100 at H100 spot rates for steps 1-3; $400 more for the optional AppWorld arm
killing_experiment.days: 9 days: 3 of harness work, 3 of runs, 3 of analysis
killing_experiment.kills_if: Dead as a claim if the pooled mean harm over all uses is under 0.02 with the bootstrap interval's upper end under 0.04 (lesson-grain degradation too small to have a shape worth a design; the footnote is the per-retrieval harm rate on ALFWorld). Dead as a ruler if the frozen-store arm shows a bin trend whose interval excludes zero (age confounded with task order; the estimator is broken), or if the $(\beta, \gamma)$ design is too collinear to separate (condition number such that the two one-at-a-time fits disagree on the sign of $\beta - 1$). Dead as an import if, with pooled harm above 0.02, every pair of bin means differs by under 0.03 and the frailty variance interval includes 0: flat and homogeneous, so burn-in, inspection and expiry all buy nothing. The headline's attribution clause dies (the shape clause stands as a different claim, reading drift) if $\beta$ stays above 1.15 after $|M|$ enters the model.

preregistered_surprise.expected: Judgment, not evidence: probability 0.4 that the hazard rises with use-age ($\beta \in [1.2, 1.8]$) and the rise is absorbed by the store-size term ($\gamma > 0$ with $\beta$ falling into $[0.9, 1.1]$ once $|M|$ is in the model); 0.35 that it is flat ($\beta \in [0.85, 1.15]$, $\gamma \approx 0$) with strong frailty; 0.25 that it falls ($\beta < 0.85$ after frailty). Probability 0.6 that the top fifth of lessons by frailty carry over half the summed positive harm. Expected mechanism: ALFWorld tasks are drawn from a fixed distribution with no fact edits, so the only thing that changes between a lesson's first and tenth use is the store around it.
preregistered_surprise.field_assumes: Four designs, four unmeasured shapes, in their own words (abstracts fetched 2026-11-15). FGSE 2611.14326 admits a lesson only after 'target-transfer, falsification, and archived-regression probes' and reports 'harmful committed updates to 3.6%' (defects at birth; burn-in). WikiTrace 2611.14320: degradation comes when the agent 'follows a lesson that is incorrect, or misapplies or misreads a valid one', inspected at every use (a per-use draw). 2610.17544: 'A contracted memory saves reasoning steps and errors until its facts change, then quietly answers wrong' (constant within an epoch). TrackRL 2610.25126: skills 'becoming redundant after the model internalizes their capabilities ... still others turning harmful', with protected incubation for young skills (the opposite sign to burn-in). Library Drift 2605.19576: 'unbounded skill accumulation without outcome-driven lifecycle management causes retrieval degradation, false-positive injections' (crowding, at library level, as pass@1 over rounds).
preregistered_surprise.belief_changing: If the rise is absorbed by store size, lesson-grain harm is crowding: capacity or age bounds are the right design, admission probing is sized by $1 - (1 - p)^{k}$ and FGSE's residual is leakage rather than a defect floor, and 2610.17544's constant-within-epoch null needs a store-size term. If the hazard is flat with strong frailty, burn-in works only as a frailty screen (for $p = 0.1$, three probes catch 27%, thirty catch 96%) and expiry buys nothing. If it falls after frailty, the first uses are the admission test, TrackRL's protected incubation has the wrong sign and WikiTrace's descent after age 3 is waste. If it rises at fixed store size, a lesson is degraded by its own age, a reading-drift mechanism no fetched source names. In every branch 'memory-induced degradation' becomes a curve over use-age with a frailty share, not one rate.

identifiability: Random given: fixed task, lesson text, store state at retrieval, actor and sampling, deterministic environment (ALFWorld returns the same verdict for the same action sequence; no environment luck term; the verifier is programmatic). Whose temperature: the actor's deployed setting, read from WikiTrace's code before the run (not in its abstract); at temperature 0 each (task, store) pair has a fixed outcome up to serving noise and $n = 1$ suffices; the writer's temperature does not enter the hazard (lesson text is fixed once written) and enters only the frailty distribution, reported as a protocol term. Whose property: $z_\ell$ belongs to the lesson text under this actor; $\lambda$ to the (store, actor, task distribution) triple; $\beta$ and $\gamma$ to the protocol (use-age is a count under top-$k$ retrieval; crowding is a property of the store growth rule, so a capacity-bounded store cannot show $\gamma$ by construction); the task order is randomised over 3 seeds so age is not a proxy for one task sequence. Degenerate-null guard: the frozen arm is flat by construction. Label noise: $\hat\delta_{\ell u}$ at $n = 4$ has standard error about $\sqrt{2q(1-q)/4} \approx 0.35$ at $q = 0.5$, symmetric under the null; the ruler is the signed bin mean (about 375 pairs per bin, bin standard error about 0.02).

scorecard.target_value: In print (abstracts fetched 2026-11-15): WikiTrace 2611.14320 (memory-induced degradation named and reduced); FGSE 2611.14326 ('when an experience-derived behavioral update should be admitted into persistent agent state'; 3.6%); 2610.32578 (a six-week ledger of 118 agent failures under rule files; 'Stale documentation (drift) was the largest failure class (48 of 118)'); TrackRL 2610.25126 (lifecycle management from per-skill counterfactual evidence); Library Drift 2605.19576 (crowding named; 'premature retirement (active harm, $-0.019$)'); 2610.17544. Who pays: builders of self-evolving memory choosing between admission probes, per-use inspection and expiry; teams running rule files and auto-memory in coding agents; evaluators who report one degradation number.

impact_ceiling.floor: pooled harm under 0.02 or no shape and no frailty: a footnote giving the per-retrieval harm of lesson-grain memory on ALFWorld and saying the four lifecycle designs are indistinguishable at benchmark scale. Requires step 1. Judgment p 0.35.
impact_ceiling.middle: a shape and a frailty share on one harness with the policy it selects (probe count from the leakage formula, or a capacity / age bound) and FGSE's residual read as leakage: a proper idea; self-evolving papers report degradation by use-age. Requires steps 1-3 with the frozen null passed. Judgment p 0.45.
impact_ceiling.ceiling: the shape replicates across harnesses (AppWorld, a coding harness with repository drift), the leakage formula predicts admission-battery residuals in two papers, and the lesson-lifecycle ruler becomes the column every self-evolving memory paper reports; a lab-adjacent standard. Requires step 4 and one more harness, $400-800. Judgment p 0.2.

scorecard.relevance: L4 all routes, Narasimhan's self-evolving interest directly (a measurement with a protocol consequence); L1 through the reliability register (hazards, replicates); L2 only as the counterfactual estimator TrackRL already uses; L3 and L5 zero. Industry: direct (coding-agent products write rules and auto-memory with no retirement policy; 2610.32578 says the stores only grow). Jacob's edge: power-law hazards, mixtures of constant-rate units reading as a falling pooled hazard, the Duane plot and the $1 - (1 - p)^{k}$ screening arithmetic are his to check by hand; the bathtub is his to say in a talk.
scorecard.kill_probe: Step 1 (about 18 GPU-hours, $60, 6 days) plus step 2 (10 GPU-hours, 2 days): dead if pooled harm is under 0.02 (upper end under 0.04); dead as a ruler if the frozen arm trends or the $(\beta, \gamma)$ fit cannot separate; dead as an import if bins agree within 0.03 and frailty variance includes 0.
scorecard.density_and_ownership: L4 is the densest lane (about 3.4 compaction-agent papers a week by the CL-W45-08 kill search's count); lifecycle papers ran at about two a month in October 2026 (TrackRL, SkillForge 2610.09832, Selm 2610.24630, 2610.32322, 2610.32578, REM 2610.27377, 2610.17544) and two more in November (WikiTrace, FGSE); this run's lifecycle query returned 226 hits with none fitting a per-lesson hazard against use-age. Occupied: lifecycle state machines with incubation and retirement (TrackRL, SkillForge), staleness as a change-point with certificates (2610.17544), crowding at library level (Library Drift), admission probing (FGSE; PACE 2606.08106, the W42 S12xF3 record), the per-lesson with/without contrast (TrackRL; CoReMem; RBC 2610.18427's randomised inclusion of playbook lessons), lessons carrying chance from lucky runs (2610.33029, 256 synthetic worlds), 'presence is not responsibility' for skill credit (GRSE 2610.27227). Unoccupied in every fetched source: the per-use harm of a lesson against its own use-age, the frailty / aging / crowding split, the frozen-store null, the burn-in leakage of an admission battery. First movers: the TrackRL authors (per-skill contrasts over training steps), the 2610.17544 authors (a ledger with use counts), the WikiTrace authors (the harness); the re-open test is asking them. Race: about two lifecycle papers a month against a 9-day probe, window at least 2x holds for the probe; Gate 2B flag: if the answer is crowding, Library Drift's authors stated the library-level version.
scorecard.why_now: WikiTrace and FGSE (2026-11-10); CoReMem (2026-11-12); TrackRL (2026-10-18); 2610.17544 (2026-10-13); 2610.33029 (2026-10-12); the survival vocabulary (Kaplan-Meier in 2610.17544) is already in the lane.
scorecard.register_and_not: Measurement: a hazard shape (four bins and a power law) with a frailty share and a crowding exponent, a mechanism (harm is a lesson property, a per-use draw, or the company a lesson keeps) and a policy consequence (probe, inspect or expire; the probe count from the leakage formula). It is not a new memory system, not an admission gate (made by PACE), not a staleness detector (2610.17544), not a library-level drift diagnosis (2605.19576), and not a run-to-run variance study: the unit is one lesson at one use.

title: The orchestrator's closed-book answer as the leak: a judge-free count of lost items whose brief or final answer carries the model's own prior, in place of the paper's attribute-addition judge

glossary.orchestrator / executor: in 2611.16526 the orchestrator is the model instance that holds the user's question, writes one brief per fact and integrates the answers; the executor is a fresh instance of the same model with the web tools that answers one brief and returns text
glossary.brief: the message the orchestrator writes down to the executor (the rewritten sub-question)
glossary.return: the message the executor writes up to the orchestrator; in the paper only its final answer ('neither the executor's intermediate trajectory nor the contents returned by its web tools', App. A)
glossary.return rate: the length in tokens of the return message; 'rate' in the rate-distortion sense (bits spent on the description)
glossary.frozen trace: an executor run stored once (queries, snippets, opened pages, HTTP failures, final answer) and replayed to the orchestrator byte-identical in every arm, so tool budget, page content and failures cannot differ across arms
glossary.knee: the smallest return rate at which the orchestrator recovers a pre-set fraction (0.8) of the accuracy gap between answer-only and full-trace returns
glossary.decoder side information: information the receiver already holds and uses to decode a message; here the orchestrator's closed-book answer, right before the model's training cutoff and wrong after it
glossary.post-cutoff: facts dated after the model's training data ends, so the model's memory of them is wrong by construction (closed-book accuracy 0.00-0.06 in the paper's Table 2)
glossary.matched loss: the single agent's accuracy minus the delegated system's accuracy when both have the same pooled tool budget and the same tool-use instruction
glossary.two-player Shapley split: the unique split of a loss between two causes (brief, return) that averages each cause's marginal effect over both orders of inclusion; efficient (the shares sum to the loss), symmetric, a dummy gets zero
glossary.delivered and ignored: evidence that was in the receiving agent's input and was not used (2611.13254's category: 'in an agent's input and was never mentioned')
glossary.closed-book answer: the model's answer to the item with no tools (the paper's no-tool arm), $b_i$; its parametric prior
glossary.brief leak: the brief contains a value (title, author, year, country, number) absent from the user's item text and present in $b_i$: the orchestrator wrote its guess into the executor's task
glossary.return override: the orchestrator's final answer equals $b_i$ and differs from the executor's answer $a_i$: it kept its own guess over the return
glossary.lost item: correct under the single agent in at least 4 of 5 runs and wrong under matched delegation $D(1,1)$ in at least 4 of 5 (C-W46-08's definition)

statement: On C-W46-08's logs and C-W46-07's closed-book arm (no extra runs), for each item $i$ with closed-book answer $b_i$, executor answer $a_i$, brief text and the orchestrator's final answer $\hat y_i$, define the brief leak $\beta_i = \mathbf{1}[\text{brief}_i \text{ holds a normalised value absent from the item text and present in } b_i]$ and the return override $\omega_i = \mathbf{1}[\hat y_i = b_i \ne a_i]$, both by deterministic normalised string match on the item's attribute fields, and compute among lost items the prior-leak share $\pi = \Pr[\beta_i \lor \omega_i \mid \text{lost}]$ separately pre- and post-cutoff, the leak rate on items delegation did not lose (the control), and the correctness of leaked brief values pre versus post (the paper's Table 3 reads $93 \to 6$ for GPT-5's medium attribute by LLM judge; here judge-free). Report alongside the single agent's own query leak (the share of first search queries carrying $b_i$), since Figure 2 shows single agents add attributes too.
claim: Post-cutoff, at least half of the items delegation loses carry the orchestrator's own closed-book answer, written into the brief or kept over a correct return: the downward distortion and the upward override are one mechanism, the parametric prior entering both messages, and the fix is to keep the prior out of both.
trick: Ask the boss the question with no tools, write down its guess, and count how often that same guess shows up in the note it sends the subagent or in the answer it keeps after the subagent comes back with something else.
why_now: 2611.16526 measured brief distortion with an LLM judge it never validated (only the same-search judge was checked against humans, App. C.1), on Books only, and measured the return side by reaction rates; its no-tool arm gives $b_i$ for every item, so the judge can be replaced by a string match against the model's own output at zero cost once C-W46-08 runs.

killing_experiment.design: Step 1 (1 day, no compute): normalisation rules per dataset (titles and authors lower-cased and stripped; years and GDP values exact; countries by ISO name); compute $\beta_i$, $\omega_i$, $\pi$ by cutoff and by model on C-W46-08's six arms, with prompt-cluster bootstrap; the control rate on non-lost items; the single agent's query leak from C-W46-07's traces. Step 2 (half a day): compare $\beta_i$ with the paper's judge on a 100-brief Books sample labelled by two humans (Cohen's $\kappa$), so the judge-free rate is calibrated once.
killing_experiment.kills_if: Dead if $\pi < 0.2$ post-cutoff on both gpt-oss-120b and GPT-5 with the interval's upper end under 0.3 (the lost items are not the prior's; the loss is a context-separation cost independent of what the model believes), or if the leak rate on lost items is within 5 points of the rate on non-lost items (the leak is a rewriting habit that does not decide outcomes, the paper's 'Query rewriting can alter the task itself' as a style fact). Dead as a ruler if the string-match $\beta_i$ agrees with the two human labels at $\kappa < 0.6$ on the Books sample.

preregistered_surprise.expected: Judgment, not evidence: probability 0.5 that $\pi \ge 0.5$ post-cutoff on both models with the leak rate on lost items at least 20 points above the non-lost rate; 0.3 that $\pi \in [0.2, 0.5)$; 0.2 that $\pi < 0.2$. Probability 0.6 that the brief leak carries more of $\pi$ than the override (the orchestrator has no tool and nothing to do with a return it doubts except re-delegate, so overriding is rarer than folding a guess into the brief).
preregistered_surprise.field_assumes: 2611.16526 treats the two sides as two findings: sec. 5.1 'Query rewriting can alter the task itself' and 'delegation adds only incorrect author information on the post-cutoff split' (Table 3, by LLM judge), and sec. 5.4 re-delegation of 6-9% of correct returns with the quoted reaction 'Subagent is wrong'; sec. 7 calls the boundary the cause. 2605.28721 (card neighbour, abstract fetched 2026-11-15 by the card run): search agents 'write most queries from internal hypotheses', the same leak for the single agent's query.
preregistered_surprise.belief_changing: If $\pi \ge 0.5$, the post-cutoff delegation loss is the orchestrator's prior entering both messages, a side-information effect rather than a boundary effect: verbatim items and evidence-bearing returns are one fix, and the paper's two failure modes collapse into one. If $\pi < 0.2$, the prior is not the leak and the loss sits in the fresh executor context or the instruction, which narrows CL-W46-03 to its budget clause.

identifiability: Random given: the parent probes' fixed logs; $b_i$ from the same model's no-tool arm at the paper's temperature ($n = 3$ draws; a brief leak counts if it matches any draw, and the match rate against the other draws is the chance floor). Whose property: $\pi$ belongs to the (model, protocol) pair and is conditioned on the lost-item set, which C-W46-08 defines by run majority; the control rate on non-lost items is the base rate the leak is read against. Verifier, not judge: string match; the human calibration is of the ruler, not of outcomes.

scorecard.target_value: In print: 2611.16526 sec. 5.1 and Table 3 (judged attribute addition; judge unvalidated, App. C.1), sec. 5.4 (re-delegation of correct returns), sec. 7; 2605.28721 (queries from internal hypotheses). Who pays: the paper's authors (a judge-free version of their rate), harness builders (whether to pass items verbatim), and the attribution line (a mechanism label computable without a judge).

impact_ceiling.floor: a judge-free replication of the paper's brief-distortion rate with its correctness split, cited as the validation the paper lacks. Requires step 1. Judgment p 0.45.
impact_ceiling.middle: the two failure modes shown to be one mechanism on two models: the prior-leak share becomes CL-W46-03's mechanism number and a reporting line for delegation studies. Requires steps 1-2. Judgment p 0.4.
impact_ceiling.ceiling: the prior-leak ruler adopted by an attribution benchmark as a judge-free mechanism label for handoff failures. Requires a second task family. Judgment p 0.15.

scorecard.relevance: L4 (the brief and the return read for what they carry of the writer's prior); L1 (a judge replaced by a verifier on a published rate); L2, L3, L5 zero. Industry: direct for harnesses that rewrite briefs. Jacob's edge: a side-information argument said plainly; otherwise none.

scorecard.density_and_ownership: Occupied: judged attribute addition (2611.16526 sec. 5.1); queries written from internal hypotheses for single agents (2605.28721); knowledge-conflict and stale-value selection in the reading model (2609.38866 stale binding, from the CL-W44-06 kill report). Unoccupied in the fetched set: a judge-free match of handoff messages against the writer's own closed-book output, on both channels, conditioned on lost items. Owner: the 2611.16526 authors hold the briefs and the no-tool outputs and can compute this tomorrow; that is the race and the reason it is a probe of CL-W46-03, not a claim.

title: The checkpoint x problem x draw table of one GRPO run: what the greedy 'forgetting' gap is made of

glossary.GRPO: group relative policy optimization: RL on a language model where a group of sampled answers to one prompt is scored and each answer's reward is compared with the group mean
glossary.checkpoint: the saved weights of the policy at one training step
glossary.greedy decode: generating with the most probable token at every step (temperature 0), one deterministic output per input
glossary.solved set $Q_i$: the validation problems whose single greedy decode at checkpoint $i$ ends in the reference answer (Agentic-OPD eq. 2)
glossary.union-versus-best gap $G$: problems some earlier checkpoint's greedy decode solved and the best-validation checkpoint's did not, $G = U_{\geq 1} \setminus Q_{\mathrm{best}}$
glossary.RL temperature: the sampling temperature the GRPO rollouts were drawn at ($T = 1.0$ in the Search-R1 recipe)
glossary.cell: one (checkpoint, problem) pair of the crossed design
glossary.coin-flip cell: a cell whose success probability under sampling at the RL temperature lies between 0.2 and 0.8
glossary.strict drop: a problem whose success probability was at least 0.8 at some earlier checkpoint and is at most 0.2 at the best one
glossary.argmax flip: a change of the greedy output between two checkpoints with no material change of the success probability, a near-tied token switching sides under a few RL steps
glossary.hidden fixed facet: generalizability theory's name for a source of variation held at one condition in every cell (here the single decoding draw), whose variance is absorbed into the interaction it sits under instead of being estimated
glossary.G-study: the generalizability study: the crossed design that estimates one variance component per facet and interaction
glossary.intraclass correlation $\\rho_1$: the share of a single draw's variance that is between-cell rather than within-cell noise
glossary.Search-R1 recipe: GRPO on Qwen2.5-3B-Instruct with a Wikipedia retriever as the tool, four turns, exact-match reward, the recipe Agentic-OPD follows and whose checkpoints are public on the Hub

statement: Train one Search-R1-recipe GRPO run (Qwen2.5-3B-Instruct, HotpotQA, 300 steps, a checkpoint every 10 steps, $n = 30$), greedy-decode every checkpoint on $N = 1{,}000$ validation problems to rebuild Agentic-OPD's greedy table, its gap set $G$ and Temporal Sampling's forgetting score, and decode $n_s = 10$ of the checkpoints (every 30 steps plus the best and the final) $m = 8$ times at $T = 1.0$ to estimate the per-cell success probability $\hat p_{ix} = \frac{1}{m}\sum_{d=1}^{m} Y_{ixd}$, with $Y_{ixd} \in \{0,1\}$ the outcome of draw $d$ of checkpoint $i$ on problem $x$. Fit the two-way table $\hat p_{ix} = \mu + \alpha_i + \beta_x + \gamma_{ix} + e_{ix}$ ($\alpha_i$ the learning curve, $\beta_x$ difficulty, $\gamma_{ix}$ problem-specific learning and forgetting, $e_{ix}$ the binomial draw error of known variance $\hat p_{ix}(1 - \hat p_{ix})/m$), subtract the binomial term from the residual, and report the components, $\rho_1$, and the split of $G$ into strict drops, coin-flip cells and argmax flips with a problem-cluster bootstrap. Random given: fixed task set, retriever index and prompt (the environment is deterministic given the action sequence), so at $T = 0$ the draw facet is zero up to serving arithmetic and the greedy gap is the argmax's checkpoint-by-problem interaction; at $T = 1.0$ the per-cell probability is the policy's quantity and the draw residual is the protocol's.
claim: At least half of the greedy gap set of a Search-R1-recipe GRPO run at 3B is coin-flip cells and at most a fifth is strict probability drops, so the union-versus-best 'forgetting' count is a protocol number until a draw floor is reported beside it.
trick: Decode a few checkpoints eight times instead of once, and count how many 'forgotten' problems are ones the policy solves about half the time at every checkpoint.
why_now: Agentic-OPD (2611.12799, 2026-11-09) turned the greedy union-versus-best gap into a training target with a teacher scheduler that reads greedy sets (eqs. 4-9), so the ruler now moves compute; Temporal Sampling (2505.20196, 2025-05-26) made the greedy forgetting score a metric and stated greedy was chosen 'to minimize variability'; Search-R1 GRPO checkpoints at Qwen2.5-3B-Instruct are public (PeterJinGo/SearchR1-nq_hotpotqa_train-qwen2.5-3b-it-em-grpo, Hub listing checked 2026-11-16), so the recipe is reproducible and the final checkpoint needs no training.

killing_experiment.design: Step 0 is C-W46-14 (about 8 GPU-h, 3 days; must run first). Step 1 (about 60-100 GPU-h training, judgment: the paper gives no figure for its 500-step run on 8 A800s; 3 days): the GRPO run above on 8 GPUs with the Search-R1 harness. Step 2 (about 40-70 GPU-h, 3 days): greedy decodes of 30 checkpoints x 1,000 problems (30,000 four-turn episodes) and $m = 8$ draws at $T = 1.0$ on 10 checkpoints x 1,000 problems (80,000 episodes) with vLLM; a two-stage replicate row (4 draws everywhere, 4 more only where the first 4 disagree) with the draw count saved at equal cell classification. Step 3 (3 days, $0): the ANOVA with the binomial correction, the gap split, $\rho_1$, the D-study curve $\rho_m = m\rho_1/(1 + (m-1)\rho_1)$, and the persistence histogram of greedy sequences (switch counts against the independent-Bernoulli reference $2(n-1)\bar Y_x(1 - \bar Y_x)$). Sensitivity rows: $m \in \{4, 8, 16\}$ on 200 problems; thresholds 0.2/0.8 and 0.3/0.7. Fallback at half the cost: Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct or 500 problems.
killing_experiment.dollars: about $350 at H100 on-demand rates; about $180 for the 1.5B fallback
killing_experiment.kills_if: Dead as 'the greedy gap is mostly protocol' if the strict-drop share of $G$ is at least 0.5 with the bootstrap interval's lower end above 0.35 at $m = 8$, $T = 1.0$: forgetting within one run is then a real problem-specific property and the greedy ruler over-counts by under 2x. Dead as a ruler if at least 90% of the 10,000 sampled cells have $\hat p_{ix} \in \{0, 1\}$: the policy is near-deterministic at the RL temperature and the draw facet is empty by the policy's own entropy (Sharpening Tax 2610.01509: post-training 'pushes tasks toward two extremes, always solved or never solved'); then the persistence statistics are the forgetting measurement and the record closes with them. Gate 0 fails for the greedy sets themselves if C-W46-14's temperature-0 disagreement across batch compositions exceeds 5% of problems.

preregistered_surprise.expected: Judgment 0.55: coin-flip share of $G$ at least 0.5 and strict drops at most 0.2; 0.25: strict drops between 0.2 and 0.5; 0.2: strict drops at least 0.5. $\rho_1$ between 0.5 and 0.8 with judgment 0.5 (0.25 above 0.8 under entropy collapse; 0.25 below 0.5). Mechanism: GRPO at 3B over four-turn retrieval leaves a wide band of problems at intermediate success probability (the paper's own LAD filter exists because $G$-sample rates on training problems are fractional, eq. 10); five RL steps move near-tied argmaxes without moving probabilities, so the greedy table flickers on exactly those problems and the first greedy success puts each into $U_{\geq 1}$ within a few checkpoints.
preregistered_surprise.field_assumes: Agentic-OPD 2611.12799 sec. 2 (card, full text): 'We use greedy decoding for all checkpoint evaluations'; its headline reads the gap as 'forgotten agent capabilities' and concedes only that 'measuring how much of the historical task coverage can be reliably recovered' is a 'useful next step' (sec. 5). Temporal Sampling 2505.20196 sec. 2.2 (import, full text): 'To minimize variability arising from different sampling methods during evaluation, we employ greedy sampling', and reads the table as 'the model oscillates between correct and incorrect answers across checkpoints' (Figure 3). Neither decodes any checkpoint twice on the forgetting set.
preregistered_surprise.belief_changing: If coin-flip cells are at least half of $G$: every checkpoint-consolidation or temporal-ensembling paper reports $\rho_1$ and $m$ beside its forgetting score, HCN-style teacher selection moves from greedy set cover to $\hat p$ differences with a replicate rule, and the recoverable target of a consolidation stage is a fifth of the headline. If strict drops are at least half: forgetting within one RL run is a large problem-specific property and the greedy ruler stands within 2x, a footnote licensing it. If the draw facet is empty: the dice sit in the optimizer's step, not the sampler, and Temporal Sampling at $T > 0$ has nothing to recover that one checkpoint's sampling would not.

scorecard.target_value: In print: Agentic-OPD sec. 5 ('reliably recovered' as a next step; 'Recovery remains incomplete ... some tasks show regressions') and its recovery accounting (60 recovered, 45 lost, net 15 of 2,000, sec. 4.3); Temporal Sampling's stated choice of greedy and its Figure 3 reading; the W46 card 2611.16315's open port of the item-versus-draw decomposition to discrete agent benchmarks (per the import record; not read by this operator). Who pays: anyone running a consolidation or temporal-ensemble stage on checkpoints, anyone reporting a forgetting score across checkpoints, anyone selecting a checkpoint from a run.

impact_ceiling.floor: Strict drops at least half, or a near-deterministic policy: a footnote licensing the greedy ruler within 2x or re-reading it as argmax churn, plus the first variance-component card for an RL run. Requires steps 0-3. Judgment 0.3.
impact_ceiling.middle: Coin-flip share at least 0.5 on one agent domain: forgetting scores and consolidation targets carry $\rho_1$ and $m$; the recoverable target is a fifth of the headline; one community (L2 training-dynamics and checkpoint-ensembling papers). Requires steps 0-3 with the two-stage replicate row. Judgment 0.5.
impact_ceiling.ceiling: The three-way split holds on a math run too (about 15 GPU-h more on a Temporal-Sampling-style 1.5B run) and probability-based consolidation matches greedy HCN at matched compute (about 60 GPU-h more): a protocol change across the checkpoint-ensembling literature. Judgment 0.2.

scorecard.relevance: Narasimhan route (Odysseus, EasyPPO train multi-turn agents and save checkpoints): direct through the training-dynamics register. Any RL group: direct (how many draws a checkpoint table needs). L1 evaluators: direct (a reliability instrument for per-checkpoint solved sets). Industry: direct for teams buying a consolidation stage. Systems route and L5: zero. Jacob's edge: variance components with a binomial correction, an intraclass identity, a Bernoulli allocation rule and a persistence statistic are checkable by hand; the hidden-fixed-facet reading of greedy is an identifiability point of the kind the live sessions produced.
scorecard.kill_probe: C-W46-14 first (about 8 GPU-h, $20, 3 days), then steps 1-3 (about 150 GPU-h, $350, 12 days); dead if the strict-drop share of $G$ is at least 0.5 (lower bound above 0.35), or 90% of cells settled at $m = 8$, or temperature-0 disagreement above 5%.
scorecard.density_and_ownership: Checkpoint-forgetting for LLM RL: 6 API hits for forgetting x checkpoints x RL x LLM (2026-11-16, sorted by date); on point only 2505.20196; 2509.12235 is a checkpoint-wise SFT-then-RL analysis ('OOD performance often peaks early during SFT and then declines') without replicates; 2602.03073 is retention under SFT. Checkpoint consolidation x RL x LLM: 16 hits, no twin of the noise-floor reading in the window (2611.12799 v2 and 2609.05295 RISE are recipes). Occupied: the greedy forgetting score and the union-versus-best gap (2505.20196, 2611.12799); Pass@k over checkpoints as a method (2505.20196); the always/never-solved sharpening reading (2610.01509, abstract fetched). Unoccupied in every fetched source: a per-cell success probability on the forgetting set, the three-way split with a reported draw floor, the persistence statistic under an empty draw facet, a replicate-allocation rule for checkpoint tables. Natural first movers: the Temporal Sampling authors, who hold $r_{i,j}$ for 8 checkpoints at 64 samples and could compute the split today; the Agentic-OPD authors with 100 checkpoints. Race window: about one relevant paper a month against a 12-day probe.
scorecard.why_now: Agentic-OPD 2026-11-09 (the greedy gap becomes a training target); Temporal Sampling 2025-05-26 (the metric); 2611.16315 2026-11-12 (the decomposition on a continuous task, per the import); public Search-R1 GRPO checkpoints and harness.
scorecard.register: Measurement: a variance-component card for one RL run, a reliability coefficient for the greedy solved set, a pre-registered split of the forgetting gap, a replicate rule; mechanism (near-tied argmaxes flip under five RL steps without moving probabilities) and consequence (what a consolidation stage can recover; how many draws a checkpoint table needs). It is not a consolidation recipe, not a critique of OPD, not a run-to-run variance study of agent scores (CL-W43-14, CL-W44-07), and not a model-size claim: the fallback at 1.5B tests the same ruler.

positioning_note: Solo: public recipe, public checkpoints, about 150 GPU-h. Lab: the Temporal Sampling or Agentic-OPD authors run the split on checkpoints they already hold in a day; a room with its own RL runs adds the replicate rule to its validation step.

title: One public checkpoint decoded twice: the noise floor under Agentic-OPD's recovery count and the coin-flip share a 3B search agent carries

glossary.noise floor: the churn two readings of the same policy show with no change of weights: the smallest difference a comparison of two checkpoints can mean anything above
glossary.batch composition: which other requests share the serving batch with a request; at temperature 0 it changes outputs only through floating-point arithmetic order (2602.07150, the pipeline's W43-W44 precedent)
glossary.coin-flip share $f$: the fraction of validation problems whose success probability under $m$ sampled decodes at the RL temperature lies between 0.2 and 0.8
glossary.stationary reference: the union-versus-final gap a policy with no forgetting at all would show if each checkpoint's greedy outcome were an independent draw with the problem's own success probability: an upper reference, not a null, because greedy outputs at fixed weights are not independent draws
glossary.recovery count: Agentic-OPD sec. 4.3: the student 'recovers 60 questions from the historical union while losing 45 previously solved questions' on 2,000 routing-validation questions, read by the paper as consolidation
glossary.exact match: the reward: the final answer string equals the reference

statement: Take the public Search-R1 GRPO checkpoint at Qwen2.5-3B-Instruct (PeterJinGo/SearchR1-nq_hotpotqa_train-qwen2.5-3b-it-em-grpo) in the Search-R1 harness on 500 HotpotQA validation problems and (a) greedy-decode it under three batch compositions (alone, batch of 16, batch of 64) to measure the temperature-0 disagreement rate $\delta_0$ between any two greedy readings, (b) decode it $m = 8$ times at $T = 1.0$ to get $\hat p_x$ per problem, the coin-flip share $f$ and $\rho_1$, and (c) compute from the $\hat p_x$ histogram the stationary reference $\mathbb{E}|G^{\mathrm{stat}}| = \sum_x (1 - \hat p_x)\bigl(1 - (1 - \hat p_x)^{n-1}\bigr)$ for $n = 100$ greedy checkpoints, beside the fully-correlated reference of zero. Arithmetic written now: a coin-flip problem can sit in the gap only if its best-checkpoint greedy decode failed, so coin-flip gap members number at most $fN$; with the paper's gap-to-final ratio of 0.62 and best-checkpoint accuracy $q \approx 0.55$, the claim's half-share needs $f \geq 0.31 q \approx 0.17$. No training; the retriever index and corpus are the public Search-R1 release.
claim: A single 3B search-agent checkpoint carries a coin-flip share above a fifth of the validation set at the RL temperature, and two greedy readings of it already disagree on about as many problems as Agentic-OPD's net recovery moved.
trick: Before asking whether an old checkpoint knew something the new one forgot, decode the new one twice and see how much it disagrees with itself.
why_now: Agentic-OPD (2026-11-09) reports a recovery of 60 gained and 45 lost of 2,000 with no reading of the same checkpoint twice; the Search-R1 GRPO checkpoint at Qwen2.5-3B-Instruct and the harness are public, so the floor costs one afternoon of decoding.

killing_experiment.design: Day 1: set up the Search-R1 harness, retriever (e5 index and wiki corpus from the release) and vLLM at 3B; day 2: 1,500 greedy episodes (3 compositions x 500) and 4,000 sampled episodes (8 x 500), four turns each, about 6 GPU-h; day 3: $\delta_0$, $f$, $\rho_1$, the stationary reference, and a sensitivity row at $T = 0.7$ (the paper's AgentGym test temperature). Report $\delta_0 \cdot 2{,}000$ beside the paper's 60 and 45.
killing_experiment.kills_if: Dead for CL-W46-05 (cheaply, before any training) if $f < 0.12$ with the bootstrap upper bound below 0.17 and $\delta_0 < 1\%$: a run like the paper's cannot have half its gap in coin-flip cells, and the gap must then be probability movement, so the G-study (C-W46-13) is not worth 150 GPU-h and the claim dies as written. Also dead at Gate 0 for the paper's greedy sets if $\delta_0 > 5\%$: the greedy table carries a serving component and 2,808 vs 4,553 cannot be reproduced on another server. Informative either way: $f$, $\rho_1$ and $\delta_0$ are the first such numbers for an RL'd search agent.

preregistered_surprise.expected: Judgment 0.6: $f$ between 0.25 and 0.45 (a 3B agent at 50-56% exact match with four-turn retrieval has many intermediate cells), $\delta_0$ under 3% (about 60 of 2,000, the size of the paper's recovery), stationary reference above 0.4 of $|Q_{\mathrm{final}}|$ (so the independence bracket alone reaches a large share of the 0.62 headline). Judgment 0.25: $f < 0.15$ (sharpened policy; the claim weakens before training). Judgment 0.15: $\delta_0 > 5\%$.
preregistered_surprise.field_assumes: Agentic-OPD sec. 4.3 reads 60 recovered and 45 lost as 'consolidation behavior'; sec. 2 uses greedy decoding 'for all checkpoint evaluations' with no repeated reading; Temporal Sampling chose greedy 'to minimize variability'.
preregistered_surprise.belief_changing: If $\delta_0 \cdot 2{,}000$ is of the order of 60, a consolidation paper's recovery count needs a same-checkpoint floor beside it; if $f$ is above a fifth, a greedy checkpoint table is a reading of coin flips on at least that many problems and the lane's forgetting scores need $m$ draws.

scorecard.target_value: The same consumers as C-W46-13, reached a week earlier for $20: the Agentic-OPD recovery accounting (sec. 4.3) and the Temporal Sampling greedy choice (sec. 2.2) are the sentences the floor is set against. Who pays: whoever is about to buy a consolidation stage on the strength of the 62% headline.

impact_ceiling.floor: A three-number note ($\delta_0$, $f$, $\rho_1$) for one public RL'd agent, cited by the G-study and by the next forgetting paper. Judgment 0.6.
impact_ceiling.middle: The stationary reference brackets the published 62% gap from below with no training, so the headline is read with a floor before C-W46-13 runs. Judgment 0.3.
impact_ceiling.ceiling: None beyond C-W46-13's: this is its step 0.

scorecard.relevance: As C-W46-13; Jacob's edge: the stationary-reference arithmetic and the Bernoulli floor are napkin identities; a first result in a weekend.
scorecard.kill_probe: About 8 GPU-h, $20, 3 days; kills CL-W46-05 if $f < 0.12$ (upper bound below 0.17) with $\delta_0 < 1\%$.
scorecard.density_and_ownership: Same searches as C-W46-13: no fetched source reports a same-checkpoint floor on a forgetting set. Occupied: the paper's greedy table and recovery count; 2602.07150 (pipeline precedent) owns temperature-0 variance as serving arithmetic in general, not on an agent checkpoint table. The Search-R1 authors hold the checkpoint; the Agentic-OPD authors hold 100.
scorecard.why_now: As C-W46-13; the public checkpoint makes it free of training.
scorecard.register: A noise-floor measurement and a bracket; the cheapest first move under CL-W46-05. It is not the G-study (no checkpoint facet), not a verdict on forgetting, and not a claim about Qwen3-4B (the paper's recovery backbone): it transfers the floor by the arithmetic above.

positioning_note: Solo: an afternoon on one GPU. Lab: the same reading on the paper's own 100 checkpoints.

headline_test: A consolidation stage's recovery count is within the floor two readings of one checkpoint show, and over a fifth of the problems a 3B search agent is graded on are coin flips at the temperature it was trained at.

title: The bound no dispatch order can beat: how much of the environment-capacity tail of an agent batch is work, at the shipped slot counts

glossary.batch makespan $T$: the wall-clock time from the first task's start to the last task's completion in a batch of agent tasks
glossary.environment capacity $C_E$: the number of tool or sandbox jobs the harness runs at once (MCP-Atlas live: 3; the official runner's default: 5)
glossary.sample concurrency $C_S$: the number of admitted tasks holding a slot in the harness from admission to completion
glossary.capacity separation: the card paper's change: two caps ($C_S$ for admitted tasks, $C_E$ for running tool jobs) instead of one
glossary.chain: one task's trajectory: $n_k$ turns, each an inference segment of duration $\tau_{k,m}$ (holds no environment slot) followed by a tool segment of duration $g_{k,m}$ (holds one slot)
glossary.critical path $\\mathrm{CP}_k$: $\sum_{m=1}^{n_k} (\tau_{k,m} + g_{k,m})$, the time chain $k$ needs with no waiting at all
glossary.slot work $W$: $\sum_k \sum_m g_{k,m}$, the total slot-seconds the batch's tool jobs need
glossary.makespan lower bound $T_{\\mathrm{LB}}$: $\max\{W / C_E,\ \max_k \mathrm{CP}_k\}$: no dispatch order of tool jobs finishes before the slots have done all the work or before the longest chain has run (the parallel-machine bound of scheduling theory, $P \mid \mathrm{chains} \mid C_{\max}$)
glossary.FCFS: first-come-first-served dispatch of pending tool jobs
glossary.CAAS: the card paper's rule: pending tool jobs sorted by 30-second arrival band, then most completed turns, then shortest mean inference time, then FCFS (eq. 16)
glossary.hindsight list schedule: a dispatch order computed with every $\tau$, $g$ and $n_k$ known in advance: longest remaining critical path first (LRCP) or largest remaining slot work first (LPT)
glossary.ordering headroom $H$: $T_{\mathrm{FCFS}} / T_{\mathrm{LB}} - 1$, an upper bound on the share of makespan any order can remove
glossary.capture ratio $\\rho$: $(T_{\mathrm{FCFS}} - T_{\mathrm{rule}}) / (T_{\mathrm{FCFS}} - T_{\mathrm{hind}})$, the share of the achievable gain a rule takes
glossary.tail share $L_5 / T$: the share of makespan between 95% and 100% of tasks completing (derived from the card's Table 3: 40% and 27% after capacity separation, 8% before)
glossary.trace replay: a discrete-event simulation that re-runs recorded chains with their recorded $\tau$ and $g$ under a chosen dispatch rule and slot count

statement: On recorded agent batches with per-turn inference and tool durations, replay the chains under $C_E \in \{3, 5, 10, 25, 50\}$ slots with $C_S$ unbounded and compute, per cell, $T_{\mathrm{FCFS}}$, $T_{\mathrm{CAAS}}$ (eq. 16 reimplemented), the hindsight list schedules $T_{\mathrm{LRCP}}$ and $T_{\mathrm{LPT}}$, a random order, the bound $T_{\mathrm{LB}}$, the headroom $H$, the capture ratio $\rho_{\mathrm{CAAS}}$ and the tail share $L_5 / T$, with 20 bootstrap resamples of chains into batches of the trace's size. Add a shedding arm that drops the longest 5% of chains by $\mathrm{CP}_k$ and report its makespan saving beside $H$, so the two levers the lane argues about (reorder the tail, or shed it as the labs do under length censoring, pressure #10) are priced on one trace. Random given: recorded durations held fixed under every order and slot count (the card paper's own replay protocol, sec. 5.1), so $H$ is a property of the (trace, $C_E$) pair and the headline names both; the live check of that assumption (tool durations at $C_E = 3$ against $C_E = 5$) is step 2.
claim: At three tool slots on MCP-Atlas-shaped batches the makespan bound no dispatch order can beat sits within 10% of FCFS, so reordering tool jobs cannot remove more than a tenth of the makespan and the 27-40% tail share is the long chains' own work; the headroom opens only as $C_E$ grows toward the number of chains, where longest-chain-first hindsight rules take most of it.
trick: Add up all the tool-seconds, divide by the number of slots, compare with the longest single task, and see whether first-come-first-served was already within a tenth of that number before anyone reorders anything.
why_now: 2611.16661 (2026-11-12) ships CAAS, compares it with FCFS only, holds every recorded duration in a replay harness that could have computed the bound, and leaves a derived tail share of 27-40% unexplained; 2609.10964 (2026-09-10, HTML read 2026-11-16) ships a second tail-aware release rule for agentic workflows with no oracle or bound in its text; the GPU-side tail literature already reports oracle-normalized numbers (TIDE 2611.17924, 2026-11-13: 'up to 97% of optimal throughput') while the environment-side tail has none.

killing_experiment.design: Step 0 ($0, 2 days): write to the 2611.16661 authors for the 495 MCP-Atlas replay records (stage sequences, recorded durations) — the re-open test and the lab arm; in parallel verify which public traces carry both inference and tool durations per turn: SWE-agent and mini-swe-agent trajectories (execution_time per step; the 2609.10964 traces report a mean tool gap of 1.3 s on SWE-bench, so this is the short-tool regime where $\max_k \mathrm{CP}_k$ binds), HAL archives (timestamps to verify), Terminal-Bench sessions with tool gaps (used in replay by 2611.02543; release to verify). Step 1 ($0, 0 GPU-h, 3 days): the discrete-event replay above on every trace obtained; the deliverable is the $H$-versus-$C_E / N$ curve with $\rho_{\mathrm{CAAS}}$, $\rho_{\mathrm{LRCP}}$ and the shedding arm on it. Step 2 (optional, about 30-50 GPU-h, judgment; MCP service keys and their rate limits are the unknown dollar line; 4 days): record own MCP-Atlas batches with an open 30B-class model under the official runner at $C_E = 3$ and $C_E = 5$ with per-turn timestamps, replay them as in step 1, and compare recorded tool durations across the two slot counts (the Gate 0 check that durations do not depend on concurrency).
killing_experiment.dollars: $0 for steps 0-1; step 2 about $150 of GPU time at spot rates plus MCP service usage (unknown)
killing_experiment.kills_if: Dead as written if $H \geq 0.25$ at $C_E = 3$ on MCP-Atlas-shaped traces (the authors' or own) with the bootstrap lower bound above 0.15: ordering is then a live lever at the shipped default and the headline flips to the pre-registered alternative (CAAS captures under 0.3 of the achievable gain), which is still the first oracle bound for the environment-side tail. Uninformative, and said so, if $T_{\mathrm{LRCP}} / T_{\mathrm{LB}} - 1 > 0.15$ at $C_E = 3$: the bracket between the bound and the best hindsight list schedule is then too wide to decide, and the next step is an exact or LP bound on the smaller trace. Dead at Gate 0 if step 2 shows recorded tool durations rising by more than 20% at the median from $C_E = 3$ to $C_E = 5$: replay then does not transfer to live batches at the shipped default.

preregistered_surprise.expected: Judgment 0.5: $H < 0.10$ at $C_E = 3$ (with about 50 admitted chains and 7 in inference per the card's Table 3, three slots are busy whenever at least three chains have a ready tool job, so idle slot-time appears only when the remaining chains number under about $C_E (1 + \bar\tau / \bar g)$ — a few chains' alternation at the very end, small against a 163-minute batch), with $\rho_{\mathrm{CAAS}}$ undefined or near 1 because the achievable gain is itself a few percent; judgment 0.3: $0.10 \leq H < 0.25$; judgment 0.2: $H \geq 0.25$ with $\rho_{\mathrm{CAAS}} < 0.3$. In every case $H$ rises with $C_E / N$ and the shedding arm removes more makespan than any reordering at $C_E = 3$ (judgment 0.7).
preregistered_surprise.field_assumes: 2611.16661 sec. 4.2 (card, full text): 'With future trajectory lengths unknown, CAAS uses completed inference turns as a proxy for potentially long trajectories'; sec. 5.3: 'Although CAAS reaches 95% completion later, it finishes the batch earlier'; sec. 5.4: the final 25 tasks 'average 27.9 and 15.6 turns' — the tail is treated as a scheduling target and never compared with a bound. 2609.10964 abstract (fetched 2026-11-16): under contention 'once submitted, those turns can no longer be reordered by the workflow-level policy, increasing tail latency' — tail latency read as lost scheduling optionality. Seer 2511.14617 abstract: rollout 'suffers from substantial long-tail latency and poor resource utilization due to inherent workload imbalance' — the GPU-side tail read as utilization loss.
preregistered_surprise.belief_changing: If $H < 0.10$ at the shipped default: the last-5% tail share is a work-distribution statistic, not a scheduling KPI; scheduling papers report $T_{\mathrm{LB}}$ and $H$ beside their gains; harness owners and RL rollout engines buy slots or shed long chains instead of reordering, and the length-censoring the labs practise (pressure #10) is read as the only lever that touches this tail. If $H \geq 0.25$: the environment-side tail is the under-exploited scheduling lever and CAAS-style observation rules capture a small share of it, which puts a longest-chain-first prior (the per-task recurrence the card paper notes in sec. 5.4) on the recipe table.

Who pays: harness owners choosing $C_E$ defaults (MCP-Atlas, tau-bench, Terminal-Bench runners), RL rollout engines with sandbox fleets (ARL-Tangram's action-level scheduling), benchmark operators paying for batch runs, and the authors of the next tail-scheduling rule.

impact_ceiling.floor: The first $H$-versus-$C_E$ curve for agent batches on public traces with the CAAS and LRCP capture ratios, cited by the card paper's v2 and the next scheduling paper. Requires steps 0-1. Judgment 0.6.
impact_ceiling.middle: A reporting rule (bound and headroom beside every makespan gain) adopted by one harness or rollout-engine paper, and a recommended $C_E$ sizing rule ($C_E$ against $N$ and $\bar g / \bar\tau$) in one harness's docs. Requires step 2 on MCP-Atlas-shaped traces. Judgment 0.3.
impact_ceiling.ceiling: The shed-versus-reorder price settles how RL rollout engines treat long trajectories (truncate, carry over as partial rollouts, or reorder) with the environment-side bound as the unit; adopted as a pre-deployment check in a framework. Requires two more workloads and a live confirmation. Judgment 0.1.

scorecard.relevance: Systems route (Lloyd, Netravali, Tri Dao): direct — a definitive comparison with an oracle bound on a rollout-engine design decision. Narasimhan route: indirect (rollout cost of agent RL). Industry: direct for anyone running agent batches against capacity-limited services. L1: indirect (benchmark run cost set by harness defaults). L2, L4, L5: zero. Jacob's edge: parallel-machine makespan bounds, list scheduling and the critical-path identity are operations research he can check by hand; the discrete-event replay is computer engineering; physics zero.

Tail-of-rollout literature: 194 hits for (makespan OR long-tail OR straggler) x (rollout OR agentic OR tool calls) x LLM, of which the on-target ones are GPU-side generation-length tails — Seer 2511.14617, APRIL 2509.18521, RhymeRL 2508.18588, TailSieve 2608.22788, RollVerify 2610.09914, ASP 2611.08864, TIDE 2611.17924 ('97% of optimal throughput' is an oracle-normalized number for GPU repurposing) — and two agentic-workflow completion-time papers without a bound: 2609.10964 (tail-aware turn release on a shared inference engine; HTML read: no 'oracle', 'hindsight', 'makespan' or slot capacity in the text; tool stages are recorded delays) and PipeSwift 2609.16491 (JCT under prefill/decode balance). Race: about two agent-scheduling papers a week in the lane, one environment-side paper a quarter; a 5-day step 1.

It is not a new scheduler, not CAAS on a new benchmark, not a verdict on the card paper's 65% (which is capacity separation, not CAAS), and not a GPU-side tail paper: the resource is the environment slot.

title: The setting the validation never named: re-scoring Genie Sim Benchmark tasks under the physics time step, solver iterations and contact offset the platform ships but does not publish

glossary.Score: Genie Sim's task metric: the mean over episodes and scored stages of the stage credit $c_{is}$ (card, sec. II-C), in $[0, 1]$.
glossary.real-sim gap: $\Delta_i = \mathrm{Sim}_i - \mathrm{Real}_i$ for one (robot, task) pair; the paper reports MAE 0.0405 over 22 pairs, the README claims 'less than 10%'.
glossary.physics time step: the interval $h$ at which the engine integrates the rigid-body equations; the paper's object study uses 1 ms, the task layer's value is not stated.
glossary.solver iterations: the number of passes the contact solver makes per step (PhysX position/velocity iterations; the paper's object study: TGS 32/1).
glossary.contact offset: the distance at which PhysX begins generating contacts before surfaces touch; SimuGuard found a collision-detection constant of this kind decisive.
glossary.repeat floor: the Score difference between two runs of the same policy at the same setting with the same initial layouts; GPU PhysX is not bit-repeatable (GPUSimBench), so this is the smallest difference that means anything.
glossary.one-at-a-time: change one setting from the shipped value, hold the rest; the attribution method 2610.32277 Table 2 published.
glossary.shipped range: the values Isaac Lab and Isaac Sim ship as defaults and the paper's own values: $h \in \{1, 4, 8.3\}$ ms; position iterations $\in \{4, 16, 32\}$; contact offset at the asset default and at twice it.

statement: Install the released Genie Sim Benchmark (Isaac Sim 6.2), read the shipped physics setting $\theta_0 = (h, N_{\mathrm{pos}}, N_{\mathrm{vel}}, d_{\mathrm{contact}}, \mathrm{GPU/CPU})$ from the benchmark runtime and the per-robot physics payloads, pick 8 contact-rich released tasks (textile, stacking, handover, drawer first) and one policy per task fine-tuned the paper's way (pi0.5 SFT on real AgiBot World episodes where the task exists there, else on the released synthetic data, flagged as sim-trained), and evaluate each policy for $n = 100$ episodes with fixed initial layouts at $\theta_0$ twice (repeat floor) and at each one-at-a-time change of $h$, $N_{\mathrm{pos}}$, $d_{\mathrm{contact}}$ and GPU/CPU within the shipped range. Report per task and knob the paired Score shift $\delta_{t,k} = \mathrm{Score}_t(\theta_k) - \mathrm{Score}_t(\theta_0)$ with its bootstrap interval, against the repeat floor and against the two validity numbers the platform publishes (MAE 0.04; 'less than 10%'); report MAE and $r$ recomputed with the paper's real column where the task is one of the 22 pairs, noting that $r$ is invariant to any shift common to all tasks.
claim: On Genie Sim Benchmark the time step and contact offset move simulated task Scores of contact-rich tasks by more than the real-to-sim discrepancy the platform claims, while solver iterations move nothing above the repeat floor — so the published validity number certifies a setting the platform never names.
trick: Take the benchmark that says 'our simulator matches the real robot to within 10 points', change the physics knobs it never told you about within the range its own engine ships, and see whether the scores move by more than 10 points.
why_now: 2611.15020 (2026-11-11) is the first validity paper to name its numerics in one layer (1 ms, TGS 32/1, solref/solimp, a 20x cross-engine swing) and report task Scores from an unnamed engine and setting in the other; Genie Sim v3.5.0 (2026-11-02, README fetched) released the benchmark with task-selected runtimes (PhysX / Newton / MuJoCo) and RoboColiseum leaderboards score policies on it; 2610.32277 (2026-10-23) published the one-at-a-time harness method with the time step decisive for sim-trained trackers; SimuGuard (2026-10-30) shipped one-parameter rerun tooling; X2Real (2026-09) is the second correlation table of the autumn (0.84). Flag: the paper's own 22 policies are not released, so the probe reads the benchmark's sensitivity with a rebuilt policy, not the paper's exact table.

killing_experiment.design: Step 0 ($0, 0 GPU-h, 2 days): bring up `geniesim docker` (Isaac Sim 6.2); list the released benchmark tasks and choose 8 contact-rich ones by a written rule (a grasp-and-transport or deformation stage in the task's stage list; textile first); read $\theta_0$ from the benchmark runtime config and `payloads/Physics/physx.usda`; record the engine per task (Isaac / Newton / MuJoCo runtimes); check whether RoboColiseum baseline weights cover the chosen tasks and whether the real AgiBot World dataset has matching tasks. Dead at step 0 if the benchmark runtime exposes no physics setting to the user. Step 1 (policies; 0-80 GPU-h, 0-5 days): if no baseline covers a task, fine-tune pi0.5 with OpenPI on the matching real AgiBot World episodes (the paper's recipe; about 10 GPU-h per task, judgment) or, where no real data exist, on the released synthetic episodes (flagged sim-trained, because a sim-trained policy can exploit $\theta_0$ and that is a different quantity). Step 2 (repeat floor; about 6 GPU-h, 1 day): 100 episodes per task at $\theta_0$, twice, same initial layouts and policy sampling seed; the floor $f_t$ is the paired Score difference; this is CL-W43-09's first datum on a shipped validated benchmark. Step 3 (sweep; about 40-60 GPU-h, 5 days): one-at-a-time from $\theta_0$: $h \in \{1, 4, 8.3\}$ ms, position iterations $\in \{4, 16, 32\}$, contact offset at default and 2x, GPU vs CPU PhysX — about 7 settings x 8 tasks x 100 episodes = 5,600 episodes at roughly 25 s each (judgment). Analysis ($0, 1 day): $\delta_{t,k}$ with a paired bootstrap over episodes; a knob 'moves' task $t$ if $|\delta_{t,k}| > \max(f_t, 1.96\,\mathrm{SE})$ and $|\delta_{t,k}| > 0.10$ (the README's claim) or $> 0.04$ (the paper's MAE), both reported; recompute MAE and $r$ against the paper's real column for the tasks among its 22 pairs. Optional step 4 (the engine as a knob, see C-W46-20).
killing_experiment.kills_if: Under every knob within the shipped range, fewer than 2 of the 8 tasks move by more than $\max(f_t, 1.96\,\mathrm{SE}, 0.04)$ and none by more than 0.10: the benchmark's silence about its numerics is harmless at Score granularity and the claim is dead; the residue is the repeat-floor table (CL-W43-09) and a note that the sim-to-sim time-step datum (2610.32277) does not transfer to real-trained policy evaluation. Also dead at step 0 if the runtime exposes no physics setting.

preregistered_surprise.expected: Judgment probability 0.5: the time step ($h$ from the shipped value to 8.3 ms) moves at least 3 of 8 tasks by more than 0.10, the textile and handover tasks first; the contact offset moves at least 2 (grasp-dependent tasks); position iterations move none above the repeat floor (consistent with 2610.32277 Table 2 and SimuGuard); GPU vs CPU moves none above the floor; the repeat floor itself is 0.02-0.05 at $n = 100$; $r$ recomputed on the 22-pair subset stays above 0.93 under every knob because the shifts are shared within a task class.
preregistered_surprise.field_assumes: Genie Sim README (fetched 2026-11-15): 'Discrepancy between simulation and real-world test results is less than 10%' with no physics setting named; 2611.15020 sec. II-C: 'Simulation evaluation uses a fixed Genie Sim experimental branch' and nothing on the engine or step; SIMPLER 2405.05941: validity from matching 'the simulator's controller and camera image'; X2Real 2609.27449: 'calibrates simulation visual and physical properties ... 0.84 linear correlation' — the real-to-sim evaluation community treats visuals, controller and assets as the validity axes and numerics as fixed infrastructure; the sim-to-sim community has the opposite datum for RL trackers (2610.32277: 'a wrong timestep').
preregistered_surprise.belief_changing: If the time step or contact offset moves Scores by more than the claimed discrepancy, a real-to-sim validity number is a property of (policy, scene, engine, setting) and every validation table and leaderboard (RoboColiseum, X2Real, SIMPLER-family) must publish the setting and a sensitivity row — a reporting rule, not a method. If nothing moves above the floor, the sim-to-sim time-step result does not transfer to real-trained policy evaluation at Score granularity, and evaluation-twin builders are entitled to treat numerics as fixed infrastructure, with a citation; either way the lane's 'silent numerics' question gets its first answer on a validated benchmark.

scorecard.target_value: In print: 2611.15020 names 1 ms / TGS 32/1 / solref-solimp and a 25.50 -> 524.61 mm engine swing at the object layer (App. D.3) and reports the task layer from an unnamed setting (sec. II-C); the README's 'less than 10%'; 2609.37771: 'success criteria and simulation settings do not fully capture how acceleration affects task execution'; 2610.32277's 'wrong timestep' datum. Who pays: RoboColiseum and Genie Sim (what to publish with a board), every evaluation-twin builder (X2Real, R2S-Eval, SIMPLER, REALM) choosing what to calibrate, engine builders (NVIDIA Isaac / Newton) whose defaults are being certified by proxy, and reviewers reading a real-to-sim correlation.

impact_ceiling.floor: A sensitivity table for one shipped validated benchmark (8 tasks x 4 knobs, with repeat floor), cited by the Genie Sim paper's v2 and by the next validity table as the reason to print the setting. Requires steps 0-3. Judgment p 0.5.
impact_ceiling.middle: A reporting rule — engine, step, iterations, contact offset and a one-at-a-time sensitivity row beside every real-to-sim correlation — adopted by one benchmark (RoboColiseum or X2Real) and asked for by reviewers; the repeat-floor column becomes CL-W43-09's shipped datum. Requires a second benchmark (X2Real on Isaac Lab-Arena) at about 60 GPU-h more. Judgment p 0.3.
impact_ceiling.ceiling: The numerics-sensitivity row is a standard column of simulated robot evaluation, and the lane's V&V triad (verification of the numerics, validation against real, model-form disagreement) is adopted as the frame for validity papers. Requires three benchmarks and an engine owner's endorsement. Judgment p 0.1.

scorecard.relevance: Robotics and learning faculty: direct (what a validated benchmark certifies). Engine builders (NVIDIA Isaac / Newton, Genesis): direct (their defaults are the knobs). Industry (AgiBot, RoboColiseum, evaluation-twin vendors): direct. HAL / evaluators: indirect, as the benchmark-validity shape. Narasimhan route: zero. Systems route (Lloyd / Netravali / Tri Dao): zero. Jacob's edge: load-bearing — time step, iteration count and contact offset are discretisation and convergence choices; the GPU/CPU repeatability floor is computer engineering; no mechanical engineering is involved.
scorecard.kill_probe: Steps 0-3: about 130 GPU-h if the policies must be built (50-70 if baseline weights cover the tasks), about $400 on cloud GPUs or $0 on owned ones, 14 days; dead if fewer than 2 of 8 tasks move by more than $\max(f_t, 1.96\,\mathrm{SE}, 0.04)$ under every knob, or at step 0 if the runtime exposes no setting.
scorecard.density_and_ownership: Exact shape (a validated real-to-sim benchmark re-scored under its own numerics, shift read against its published validity number): 0 found — the 10-hit real-to-sim x numerics conjunction (API, 2026-11-15) holds no such paper by title. Coarser shapes occupied: one-at-a-time knob attribution for sim-trained RL (2610.32277 Table 2: 'solver iterations ... less than 0.006 rad', time step decisive); one-parameter reruns of benchmark rollouts (SimuGuard: collision constant decisive, 89% -> 98%); benchmark settings reversing VLA rankings (2609.37771: checkers and masses, 'bug fixes can reverse method rankings'); cross-platform VLA validity (2606.10366). Pre-window precedents: Erez-Tassa-Todorov ICRA 2015 (speed vs accuracy per engine), Kadian 2019 (sim-trained agents exploit the simulator, correlation 0.18). Owners: Genie Sim / AgiBot have the policies and the real column; the 2610.32277 authors have the harness method; neither has a reason to run it against their own validity number. Density counted at the kill search with the role words in gate6.
scorecard.why_now: 2611.15020 (2026-11-11); Genie Sim v3.5.0 benchmark release (2026-11-02) with task-selected runtimes; RoboColiseum boards (2026-06); 2610.32277 (2026-10-23); SimuGuard (2026-10-30); X2Real (2026-09). Flag: the paper's own policies are unreleased, so the shift is measured on a rebuilt policy.
scorecard.register_and_not: Measurement of a shipped artifact with a reporting consequence (print the setting, add the sensitivity row). It is not a new benchmark, not a calibration method, not an exploit claim (the policies are real-trained where possible), not a retraining 2x2 (CL-W44-08, killed), and not a claim that the engine is wrong — only that the validity number is conditional on a setting nobody can read.

identifiability: Random given: fixed policy weights and a fixed per-episode sampling seed (pi0.5's flow-matching noise is the policy's own temperature; it is pinned per episode so paired settings share it until the physics diverges), fixed initial layouts per episode index, one engine build and one GPU type; the Score shift $\delta_{t,k}$ is a property of (policy, task layout set, setting pair, engine build), and the headline names the setting levels. GPU PhysX non-determinism is measured, not assumed (step 2); common random numbers cannot couple diverging contact sequences (checklist 2026-11-08), so the paired design is by episode index and the floor is empirical. $r$ is invariant to an affine change of the simulated column, so a uniform shift leaves $r$ at 0.9686 while MAE moves; the probe reads $\delta_{t,k}$ and MAE, not $r$. Judge and verifier: the benchmark's automatic stage scorer is the verifier in every arm; no LLM judge; the manual real scoring (sec. II-C) is untouched.
positioning_note: Solo: released benchmark, assets, URDFs and either baseline weights or a pi0.5 fine-tune on public AgiBot World data; 50-130 GPU-h. Lab (AgiBot / Genie Sim or an engine owner): the same sweep on the paper's own 22 policies with the real column in hand, one week, and standing to add the setting to the board.
neighbors_checked: 2611.15020 (card, full text) — the 22-pair real-sim Score table (r = 0.9686, MAE 0.0405) computed on 'a fixed Genie Sim experimental branch' with no engine, time step or solver setting named for the task layer; the object layer names 1 ms steps, PhysX TGS 32/1 iterations and MuJoCo solref/solimp and shows one engine swap at identical parameters moving error 25.50 to 524.61 mm (App. D.3).

2610.32277 (abstract fetched 2026-11-15; full text in data/reports/2026-W45-kill-CL-W44-08.md) — RL humanoid trackers checked in a CPU MuJoCo harness: 'the first sim-to-sim gap we saw came from the harness, a missing floor and a wrong timestep, and not from the physics engines'; Table 2 one-at-a-time: solver iterations 0.577 -> 0.577 rad, time step 2 ms for 5 ms -> 1.719. Sim-trained RL, tracking error, one robot; no real column, no benchmark validity number.

2610.41857 SimuGuard (abstract fetched 2026-11-15) — per-step audit of LIBERO / RoboTwin / RoboCasa / RoboDojo rollouts; reruns 'with one simulation parameter changed'; a collision-detection constant moves five-task success 89% to 98%.
