title: Ninety-eight numbers per arm, which ones moved the task? One-group-at-a-time revert of Genie Sim's robot identification read on the task Score

glossary.identified model: the G2 crsB arm model with 98 unknowns per arm fitted from motor current (70 inertial parameters, 7 armatures, 14 friction coefficients, 7 torque offsets; card eq. 1) plus per-joint PD servo gains $K_{p,j}, K_{d,j}$ (Table C3) and the motion-controller command shaping (5 Hz Butterworth, 11 ms command period).
glossary.URDF model: the CAD-derived model before identification; the paper's 'before' column (Table B2).
glossary.parameter group: one of five sets reverted together: inertial $\boldsymbol{\pi}$, armature $\mathbf{J}_a$, friction $(f_c, f_v)$, servo gains $(K_p, K_d)$, command shaping (filter and period).
glossary.elementary effect: design-of-experiments term (Morris 1991): the change in the response when one factor moves from the baseline with the others held; here the Score change when one group is reverted.
glossary.repeat floor: as in C-W46-18: the Score difference between two identical runs.

statement: Check at step 0 whether the released G2 physics payload carries the identified values printed in Tables 3-4 and C3 (if so the identified model is released; the URDF is the 'before'), then for the released tasks among the paper's 14 G2/Arx pairs evaluate one policy per task (shared with C-W46-18) for $n = 100$ fixed-layout episodes at the identified model and at each one-group-at-a-time revert to the URDF or default value — inertial, armature, friction, servo gains, command shaping — on the benchmark's shipped physics setting. Report per task the elementary effect $\delta_{t,g} = \mathrm{Score}_t(\text{group } g \text{ reverted}) - \mathrm{Score}_t(\text{identified})$ with its paired bootstrap interval against the repeat floor, the concentration $\max_g |\delta_{t,g}| / \sum_g |\delta_{t,g}|$, and the comparison with the paper's own before/after change (MAE 0.0554 to 0.0443 on 14 pairs, 8 shrink / 1 grow / 5 unchanged).
claim: Of the 98 mechanical parameters per arm Genie Sim identified, none moves a task Score above the repeat floor; whatever the identification bought at task level sits in the three controller numbers per joint (servo gains and command shaping), so for a position-controlled arm evaluated by a VLA the calibration worth doing is the controller, not the dynamics.
trick: Put the identified arm back to its CAD values one parameter family at a time and watch the task score: if the score only moves when you touch the servo gains, the 98-parameter identification was decoration.
why_now: 2611.15020 (2026-11-11) printed a full three-stage identification (Tables 3, 4, C1-C3) with a measured task-level before/after that its own text declines to credit ('These robot-level evaluations do not establish an asset-linked benchmark benefit', sec. IV-A; 'Successful execution alone therefore cannot establish an identification benefit', sec. IV-B3); the G2 URDF/USD and per-engine physics payloads are released (README, 2026-11-02); CL-W45-J01 (2026-11-03) asked the per-parameter value question for scene parameters and left the robot class unasked. Flag: the paper's 14 policies are unreleased, so the groups are read on a rebuilt policy.

killing_experiment.design: Step 0 ($0, 1 day): diff the released G2 `robot.usda` / `payloads/Physics/*.usda` against Tables 3-4 and C3 (armature 1.5 / 0.57 / 0.29 kg m^2 groups; $K_p$ 925 ... 200; friction coefficients); if the released payload carries the identified values, the identified model is a released artefact and the URDF is the 'before'; if not, build the identified model from the printed tables where complete (armature, friction, gains, shaping are printed; the 70 inertial parameters are in Tables C1-C2 'complete joint/family breakdown' — check completeness) and cost the inertial group as unbuildable if the table is partial. Arithmetic now ($0): the paper's MAE drop of 0.011 over 14 pairs lies below the per-pair binomial-bound SE (0.05-0.09) and near the SE of the 14-pair mean (about 0.017); the sign test 8 shrink / 1 grow (ties dropped) gives $p \approx 0.04$ — marginal, so the direction is weakly in print and the attribution is not. Step 1 (policies; shared with C-W46-18, 0-60 GPU-h): the released tasks among the 14 G2/Arx pairs, pi0.5 SFT on real AgiBot World episodes where they exist. Step 2 (about 30-40 GPU-h, 4 days): 6 arms (identified + 5 reverts) x up to 8 tasks x 100 episodes with fixed layouts; the repeat floor from C-W46-18 step 2 or run here (6 GPU-h). Analysis ($0, 1 day): $\delta_{t,g}$, paired bootstrap, concentration, and a Morris-style ranking of groups by $|\delta|$ across tasks.
killing_experiment.kills_if: Every group, including servo gains and command shaping, moves every task Score by less than $\max(f_t, 1.96\,\mathrm{SE})$: the identification's task-level effect is inside the engine's own noise for all 98 + controller numbers, the paper's hedge is confirmed numerically and there is nothing to concentrate — dead as a value-concentration probe (the residue is a footnote: the published before/after improvement is a re-run noise number). Also dead if the mechanical groups move Scores by more than the controller group on most tasks (the pre-registered direction is reversed; CL-W45-J01's robot-class extension is then false, which is informative for the claim). Dead at step 0 if neither the payload nor the printed tables give a buildable identified model.

preregistered_surprise.expected: Judgment probability 0.5: servo gains and command shaping move at least 2 of the tasks by more than 0.05 (handover, stacking, place-into-drawer — timing- and overshoot-sensitive stages), friction moves at most one, armature and inertial groups move none above the floor; concentration above 0.6 on the controller group where any effect exists; the paper's 0.011 MAE drop is not reproduced above the floor by the mechanical groups.
preregistered_surprise.field_assumes: 2611.15020 sec. IV-A: 'These robot-level evaluations do not establish an asset-linked benchmark benefit' and sec. IV-B3: 'Successful execution alone therefore cannot establish an identification benefit' — the authors decline to attribute; the real-to-sim practice, SIMPLER 2405.05941 (card neighbour), calibrates 'the simulator's controller' and the camera and skips arm dynamics; the system-identification lineage (figaroh-plus, dynamic_calibration, RPNA — the paper's own cited toolboxes) assumes torque-level fit is the goal; nobody in the fetched set prints a per-group task-level value for a manipulator identification (API conjunction identification x task success x manipulation x policy: 4 hits, none on the shape, 2026-11-15).
preregistered_surprise.belief_changing: If only the controller group moves the Score, benchmark builders spend their identification budget on $K_p, K_d$ and command shaping (three numbers per joint, identifiable from one step response) and drop the 98-parameter fit for VLA evaluation — CL-W45-J01's concentration claim holds for the robot class too. If the mechanical groups move it, position-controlled VLA evaluation is sensitive to arm dynamics after all and SIMPLER-style controller-only calibration is insufficient — a datum against the current practice.

title: The engine swing at the task layer: the same Genie Sim task and policy on the PhysX and Newton runtimes the platform ships, read against the real-sim gap

glossary.model-form disagreement: the lane's third V&V leg — the difference between two engines' outputs on the same scene at identical physical parameters; the paper measured it at the object layer (sponge 25.50 mm in MuJoCo, 524.61 mm in PhysX, App. D.3) and never at the task layer.
glossary.task-selected runtime: Genie Sim's per-task choice of engine: 'direct Isaac evaluation, managed Newton wok evaluation, and native MuJoCo Rubik execution' (README).
glossary.per-engine physics payload: the AS3 asset layout's `payloads/Physics/{physics,physx,mujoco}.usda`: one robot description with engine-specific physics files (README).

statement: At step 0 list the released benchmark tasks that already carry two runtime payloads (PhysX and Newton, or PhysX and MuJoCo) and choose up to 6 contact-rich ones; where a chosen task has one runtime, port it to the second at identical physical parameters only if the port is a configuration change (no new assets), else drop it. Evaluate one policy per task (shared with C-W46-18) for $n = 100$ fixed-layout episodes on each runtime at that runtime's shipped setting and report the cross-engine Score disagreement $\epsilon_t = \mathrm{Score}_t(\mathrm{engine\ B}) - \mathrm{Score}_t(\mathrm{engine\ A})$ with its paired bootstrap interval against the repeat floor of each engine and against the paper's real-sim gap for that task where it is one of the 22 pairs.
claim: On Genie Sim Benchmark, swapping the shipped engine at identical physical parameters moves the simulated Score of contact-rich tasks by more than the published real-sim gap for those tasks, so which engine scored a task is part of the validity number and the benchmark does not say which it was.
trick: The paper showed one sponge going from 2.5 cm wrong to 52 cm wrong when the engine changed and the parameters did not; run the whole task on both engines the platform ships and see whether the task score moves more than the real-sim gap the paper reports.
why_now: Genie Sim v3.5.0 (2026-11-02, README fetched) ships task-selected runtimes and per-engine physics payloads, so an engine swap on a validated benchmark task is a configuration change for the first time; 2611.15020 (2026-11-11) measured the object-layer swing and named the task-layer engine nowhere; Alloy 2611.16312 (2026-11-12) and HolidayFactory 2611.11789 (2026-11-09) are two more Newton-based engines arriving under robot benchmarks this week, so the engine behind a Score is becoming a free variable.

killing_experiment.design: Step 0 ($0, 2 days): from the released task list and `payloads/Physics/`, count tasks with two runtimes; read each runtime's shipped setting; write the pre-registered task set (up to 6, contact-rich first; the wok task if it is the Newton one). Dead at step 0 if fewer than 3 released tasks run on two runtimes without new assets. Step 1 (policies; shared with C-W46-18). Step 2 (about 12-18 GPU-h, 3 days): 2 engines x 6 tasks x 100 episodes plus a repeat run per engine (another 12 GPU-h if not already in C-W46-18). Analysis ($0, 1 day): $\epsilon_t$ with paired bootstrap; a task 'disagrees' if $|\epsilon_t| > \max(f_t^A, f_t^B, 1.96\,\mathrm{SE})$; compare with the paper's $|\Delta_t|$ (0.00-0.11) and MAE 0.04.
killing_experiment.kills_if: On every two-runtime task $|\epsilon_t|$ is below $\max(f_t^A, f_t^B, 1.96\,\mathrm{SE})$ or below the paper's real-sim gap for that task: model-form error is inside the validation's own gap at Score granularity and the engine's name is a footnote. Also dead at step 0 if fewer than 3 released tasks run on two runtimes without porting assets (then the probe is a build, not a measurement, and is parked with that trigger).

preregistered_surprise.expected: Judgment probability 0.45: on textile or deformable tasks (where the Newton path exists because PhysX lacks cloth) the swap is not even possible at identical parameters, so the measurable set is rigid contact-rich tasks (stacking, handover, drawer); there $|\epsilon_t| > 0.10$ on at least 2 of the measurable tasks, driven by contact-offset and friction-model differences, with pick-and-place tasks inside the floor.
preregistered_surprise.field_assumes: 2611.15020 App. D.3: 'The source path does not express MuJoCo solref/solimp equivalently ... Geometry, initialization, robot/observation calibration and numerical differences remain potential contributors' — the authors treat the object-layer swing as a mapping problem, not as a property of the task Scores; the README quotes one '<10%' discrepancy for the whole benchmark across three runtimes; PolySim 2510.01708 and ROBOGATE (CL-W43-J04 kill record) measured cross-engine gaps for sim-trained RL policies, where exploitation of the training engine is the mechanism; for real-trained policies evaluated across platforms, 2606.10366 compared different platforms with different assets, not one scene with the engine swapped.
preregistered_surprise.belief_changing: If the task-layer swing exceeds the real-sim gap, a validity correlation is engine-conditional and the engine (with version) is printed with every Score and board; the lane's model-form leg has its first task-level number on a validated benchmark. If the swing is inside the floor on every measurable task, rigid-contact model-form error is a non-issue for VLA evaluation at Score granularity and the object-layer swing does not propagate — a datum the engine builders cite.

title: One public checkpoint decoded sixteen times: the coin-flip pool under a greedy forgetting gap, the serving floor of the greedy ruler, and the misclassification matrix of a band classification (v2: designed after the concept-level kill search of CL-W46-05; one-sided kill of the coin-flip clause; the drop clause is out of reach of one checkpoint and says so; after the design red team of 2026-11-15: full-dev greedy arm, operational serving arms, five-way partition, break-even gap ratio rho*, letter to the data owners)
glossary: Checkpoint: the saved weights at one training step. Greedy decode ($T = 0$): one deterministic output per input, the most probable token at every step. RL temperature: the sampling setting the policy was trained under; for Search-R1 it is temperature 1.0 and top-$p$ 1.0 (2503.09516v5 sec. 4.3 and App. B.2, fetched 2026-11-16). Success probability $p_x$: the probability that one sampled four-turn episode of the fixed checkpoint on problem $x$ ends in an exact-match answer; $\hat p_x = X_x / m$ its estimate from $m$ draws with $X_x \sim \mathrm{Bin}(m, p_x)$. Band: low if $\hat p_x \leq 0.2$, coin flip (mid) if $0.2 < \hat p_x < 0.8$, high if $\hat p_x \geq 0.8$; the true band is the same rule on $p_x$. Misclassification matrix: $\Pr[\text{band} \mid p_x, m]$, the probability that a cell of true probability $p_x$ is labelled each band from $m$ draws (binomial arithmetic, written below). Corrected band share: the share under the nonparametric maximum-likelihood mixing distribution of $p_x$ fitted to the counts $X_x$ (Kiefer-Wolfowitz NPMLE by EM on a 100-point grid), which inverts the misclassification matrix without assuming a parametric form; the raw share is reported beside it. Greedy accuracy $q$: the share of problems the greedy decode solves. Coin-flip pool $A$: the share of problems whose true band is mid and whose greedy decode fails; every coin-flip member of a greedy forgetting gap is in this pool, so $A N$ bounds the gap's coin-flip count from above. Forgetting gap $G$: in Agentic-OPD's ruler, problems some checkpoint's greedy decode solved that the best checkpoint's did not; $|G| = \rho\, q N$ with $\rho$ the gap-to-best ratio, in print as $4{,}553 / 2{,}808 - 1 = 0.62$ for $U_{\geq 3}$ against the final checkpoint (2611.12799 sec. 2). Serving floor $\delta_0$: the share of problems on which two greedy decodes of the same weights under different serving-batch compositions disagree in exact-match outcome; at $T = 0$ the policy has zero decision variance by construction, so $\delta_0$ is the serving stack's floating-point arithmetic (2602.07150 precedent). Zero-variance group: a set of $K$ sampled episodes of one problem that are all-correct or all-wrong (2606.10709's term). Split-half: draws $1$-$8$ versus $9$-$16$ of the same checkpoint. Exact match: the release's reward function (normalised string equality of the extracted answer with any reference), read from the release at step 0.
statement: Take the public Search-R1 GRPO checkpoint PeterJinGo/SearchR1-nq_hotpotqa_train-qwen2.5-3b-it-em-grpo-v0.3 (Hub listing fetched 2026-11-16: three safetensors shards, 13.6 GB, last modified 2025-05-21; the unversioned v0.1 repository, 2025-03-12, is the secondary arm) in the Search-R1 harness (E5 retriever over the 2018 Wikipedia dump, top-3 passages, at most four search turns, the Table 1 template, exact-match reward) on HotpotQA dev: the greedy batch-64 arm on the full dev set (size read from the release's data file at step 0; about 7,400), every other arm on $N = 1{,}000$ questions drawn once with seed 20261115 and committed before any GPU is used. (a) Greedy-decode ($T = 0$) under three named serving configurations of one pinned vLLM build (alone: max_num_seqs 1, one request at a time; capped at 16 and at 64 with a fixed logged submission order, prefix caching and chunked prefill off) and record $\delta_0$ (exact-match disagreement between configurations; a within-stack floor and a lower bound on the cross-server disagreement the paper's tables carry) and $q$. (b) Decode every question $m = 16$ times at temperature 1.0, top-$p$ 1.0 (the training setting), record $X_x$, the raw and corrected band shares, the coin-flip pool $A$ and the ratio $A / q$ with the break-even gap ratio $\rho^{*} = 2A / q$, the same-checkpoint zero-variance flip rate between disjoint groups of $K = 4$ and $K = 8$, the share of greedy failures on cells with $p_x \geq 0.8$ (the one-checkpoint term of the five-way partition), and the split of mid-band failures into missing-answer episodes and wrong answers (a diagnostic; $p_x$ keeps format failures, as the reward did). Harness calibrations, not findings: split-half band agreement (draws 1-8 vs 9-16) against the binomial prediction, and the cross-half covariance of $\hat p$ against the NPMLE variance. (c) Report the full partition of greedy failures by true band beside the binomial misclassification matrix at $m = 8$ and $m = 16$. Pre-registered kill of CL-W46-05's coin-flip clause under the stated transfer assumption: the claim needs at least half of $G$ in the coin-flip band, and coin-flip gap members are at most $A N$, so the claim is dead if the 95% upper bound of $\hat A$ (corrected; raw $m = 8$ and $m = 16$ within 0.03 of it) is below $0.5\,\rho\,\hat q$ with $\rho = 0.62$, the only gap ratio in print for this recipe and conservative for the claim (the claim's $U_{\geq 1}$-against-best ratio is larger; rows at $\rho = 1.0$ and $1.5$). The kill is conditional on the released final-or-last-stable checkpoint standing for the recipe's best checkpoints in band width; the claim's own run is not public. A pool above the line is 'not killed; $\rho^{*}$ reported', never support. At the in-print $q = 0.331$ (2503.09516v5 Table 3, HotpotQA, Qwen2.5-3B-Instruct GRPO) the line is $A < 0.103$. The strict-drop clause (at most a fifth of $G$ are cells above 0.8 at an earlier checkpoint and below 0.2 at the best) is not testable on one checkpoint and this probe says so: it reports only the trivial pool bound (low-band greedy failures). Optional step 4 (about 6 GPU-h): the same decodes on the v0.1 sibling, giving the first three-way split with a draw floor of a between-policy greedy disagreement set and the 2609.22547 placebo run end to end; it rehearses C-W46-13's analysis and tests no clause of the claim (two recipe versions are not two checkpoints of one run).

CL-W46-05a (coin-flip share).headline: On a Search-R1-recipe GRPO run (Qwen2.5-3B-Instruct, HotpotQA, four turns), at least half of the problems in the greedy union-versus-best gap are coin-flip cells: success probability between 0.2 and 0.8 at the best checkpoint at the training temperature, the band estimated from at least 16 sampled decodes and the share corrected for binomial misclassification.
CL-W46-05a (coin-flip share).what_it_is: A statement about the gap set of a run this probe does not have. What one checkpoint gives is the necessary condition: coin-flip gap members $\subseteq \{x : 0.2 < p_x < 0.8,\ g_x = 0\}$, whose share is $A$; with $|G| = \rho q N$, the clause requires $A \geq 0.5 \rho q$. The probe is one-sided: it can kill the clause and can report that the pool suffices, never that the clause holds.
CL-W46-05a (coin-flip share).kill: Dead if $\hat A_{\mathrm{corr}} + 1.96\,\mathrm{SE} < 0.5 \cdot 0.62 \cdot \hat q$ on the primary checkpoint (at $\hat q = 0.33$: $\hat A$ below about 0.08 at $N = 1{,}000$), and the raw $\hat A$ at $m = 8$ and $m = 16$ agree with the corrected one within 0.03. Not killed otherwise: the record reports $\hat A / \hat q$ with its band and $\rho^{*} = 2 \hat A / \hat q$, the largest gap-to-best ratio whose coin-flip half the pool can fill; at $\rho = 1.0$ the pool must be $0.5 q$, at $1.5$, $0.75 q$. C-W46-13 decides; the letter (step 0c) asks the Agentic-OPD authors for $|U_{\geq 1}|$ and $|Q_{\mathrm{best}}|$, which fixes $\rho$. Transfer assumption stated in `identifiability`.

CL-W46-05b (strict-drop share).headline: On the same run, at most a fifth of the gap's problems are strict probability drops: success probability at or above 0.8 at some earlier checkpoint and at or below 0.2 at the best.
CL-W46-05b (strict-drop share).what_it_is: A statement about two checkpoints of one run. Five-way partition of a gap member (greedy fails at best, some earlier greedy succeeded) by $p_{\mathrm{best}}$ and history: (a) $p_{\mathrm{best}} \geq 0.8$, argmax flip of a settled-high cell; (b) $0.2 < p_{\mathrm{best}} < 0.8$, coin flip; (c1) $p_{\mathrm{best}} \leq 0.2$ with some earlier $p_i \geq 0.8$, strict drop; (c2) $p_{\mathrm{best}} \leq 0.2$ with earlier successes from $0.2 < p_i < 0.8$ cells, soft drop (real movement, recoverable, not a strict drop); (c3) every $p_i \leq 0.2$, a lucky earlier greedy on a settled-low cell. One checkpoint measures (a) and the pool for (b); (c1)-(c3) need the trajectory. The trivial bound here, $B = $ share with $p_x \leq 0.2$ and $g_x = 0$, is 0.7-0.9 of all greedy failures in simulation and says nothing. Not tested here.
CL-W46-05b (strict-drop share).kill: None from this probe. The cheapest within-run second checkpoint: none is public (Hub listing 2026-11-16: 42 PeterJinGo repositories, all single-revision final checkpoints of recipe versions v0.1 / v0.2 / v0.3 by base, size and algorithm; no step folders); the options are C-W46-13's own run (about 150 GPU-h), a 50-step GRPO continuation from the public checkpoint saving every 5 steps (30-50 GPU-h, judgment; Search-R1 states 8 H100s and no step time), or the data owners (Agentic-OPD: 100 checkpoints; Temporal Sampling: 8 checkpoints with 64 samples).

G0 (Gate 0 of the greedy ruler; not a cl.headline: Two greedy readings of the same weights under different serving batches disagree on under 5% of HotpotQA problems.
G0 (Gate 0 of the greedy ruler; not a cl.what_it_is: The serving floor of Agentic-OPD's and Temporal Sampling's greedy tables: at $T = 0$ the decision variance is zero by construction, so $\delta_0$ is the floating-point order of the batch (2602.07150: SD above 1.5 points at $T = 0$ on SWE-bench).
G0 (Gate 0 of the greedy ruler; not a cl.kill: If $\delta_0 > 5\%$ the greedy checkpoint table carries a serving component and the paper's 2,808 vs 4,553 cannot be reproduced on another server (Gate 0 flag on the ruler, not on the claim). $\delta_0$ is reported beside the paper's 60 recovered / 45 lost of 2,000 as $2{,}000\,\delta_0$.

author=PeterJinGo: 42 model repositories, all final checkpoints (SearchR1-nq_hotpotqa_train-{qwen2.5-3b,7b,14b,32b,llama3.2-3b}{,-it}-em-{grpo,ppo}{,-v0.2,-v0.3}, R1 ablations, groupsize variants); 3b-it-em-grpo exists unversioned (lastModified 2025-03-12), -v0.2 and -v0.3 (2025-05-21; 3 shards 4.98 + 4.93 + 3.67 GB; config, tokenizer; no model card). No intermediate-step checkpoint of any run is listed.

gate4_hypothesis.mechanism_sentence: GRPO at 3B over four-turn retrieval leaves a wide band of problems at intermediate success probability at the training temperature (the policy's own groups of 5 were signal-bearing there, which is where its gradient came from); on such a problem the greedy argmax path is a near-tie, so small parameter moves flip it, and the first greedy success puts the problem into the union while the best checkpoint's greedy decode fails with no probability change behind it. The public checkpoint measures the band's width and the pool $A$; the flip rate between checkpoints is C-W46-13's.

consequence_per_outcome.pool_sufficient (A >= 0.31 q): The claim survives to C-W46-13 (its design red team is owed); the band is wide enough that a draw floor beside every forgetting score is a live request; the transfer caveat stays in the record.
consequence_per_outcome.kill (A_upper < 0.31 q): CL-W46-05 is dead as written (parked with the re-open trigger 'a run whose best checkpoint has a wider band', which 2610.01509 App. C.2 predicts for smaller or less-trained policies); the greedy gap of a 3B search agent is then probability movement or argmax churn of settled cells, and C-W46-13's 150 GPU-h are not spent; the result is a footnote: the first band histogram and serving floor for a public RL'd search agent, cited by the next forgetting paper.
consequence_per_outcome.format diagnostic (most mid-band failure: $p_x$ keeps them (the em reward scored them 0 in every GRPO group the optimiser saw; 2505.15117 Table 1 separates outcome-only from format-reward runs and the Hub names are -em-), so the claim is not reworded; the reading is that the lane's remedy for such cells is answer extraction or a format reward (the recipe owners' own fix, 2505.15117 sec. 4.1), not teacher selection.
consequence_per_outcome.greedy below its own mode (over 2% of gr: A finding about greedy decoding in a four-turn loop on its own: term (a) of the partition is non-trivial and every greedy checkpoint table carries it; C-W46-13 must report (a) beside the coin-flip and drop terms.
consequence_per_outcome.serving floor large (delta_0 > 5%): Gate 0 flag on the greedy ruler itself: every between-checkpoint greedy difference below delta_0 N is serving arithmetic; the paper's 60/45 of 2,000 is compared to 2,000 delta_0 in print.

trick: Before asking whether an old checkpoint knew something the new one forgot, decode the new one sixteen times at its training temperature and count how many of its greedy failures are coin flips; if there are not enough of them to fill half the published gap, the gap is not coin flips.
why_now: Agentic-OPD (2026-11-09) made the greedy union-versus-best gap a training target; 2609.22547 (2026-09-18) published the same-checkpoint placebo statistic; 2606.10709 (2026-06-09) wrote the direction (finite-group status is stochastic) for a search agent without a share; the Search-R1 3B GRPO checkpoints, retriever index and harness are public (Hub listing 2026-11-16), so the pool bound costs one day of decoding and no training.

killing_experiment.design: Step 0 (0 GPU-h, day 1 plus the download, CPU): read the verl validation decoding setting in the release's training script (the paper text states none; the reference script infer.py samples at 0.7), the reward function (qa_em: last <answer> match, strict, normalised exact match; a missing tag scores 0 and is the probe's 'missing-answer' event), the flat E5 index format and file size (the training retriever is 'E5 (exact)', 2505.15117 App. G.1; HNSW is not used because it changes the environment), the v0.1 -> v0.3 release notes (docs/experiment_log.md: v0.2 fixed retrieved-token masking and GRPO sample indexing, lengthened training; v0.3 is the 2505.15117 study), the public wandb run of the 3B-it GRPO v0.3 (steps completed; collapse or not; which rule produced the release; whether any per-prompt artefact exists), and the HotpotQA dev file (size recorded); draw the $N = 1{,}000$ question ids with seed 20261115 and commit the list before any GPU is used; write the misclassification matrix and the kill line $0.31\,\hat q$ into the analysis script with the in-print $q = 0.331$ as the expected value. Step 0c (day 1): letter to the Agentic-OPD authors asking for $|U_{\geq 1}|$, $|Q_{\mathrm{best}}|$ and the validation size of the HotpotQA-only run, for sixteen sampled decodes at temperature 1 on the gap set at the best checkpoint, and whether a v2 adds a draw floor; a note to the Temporal Sampling authors asking whether the 64 samples on 8 checkpoints will be released. No waiting rule: the probe is about 8 GPU-h, so steps 1-3 run at once and an answer later replaces the transfer assumption with the owners' numbers. Download the corpus and flat E5 index (tens of GB per the README's download script) and start the retrieval server: faiss flat on CPU (index about 65 GB in float32, judgment from about 21M passages at 768 dimensions; a machine with at least 96 GB RAM; about 0.1-0.3 s per query on 32 cores, at most 80,000 queries in steps 1-2, 3-7 CPU-hours overlapped with decoding) or faiss-gpu on a second GPU (+2 GPU-h). Step 1 (about 5 GPU-h, day 2): vLLM at 3B, pinned build, bf16, prefix caching and chunked prefill off, the Table 1 template, four search turns, top-3 passages; greedy ($T = 0$): (alone) max_num_seqs 1 on the 1,000-question subset (about 4 s per turn, about 4.5 GPU-h wall-clock, the reproducible reference); (16) max_num_seqs 16 on the subset; (64) max_num_seqs 64 on the full dev set (about 1 GPU-h; $\hat q$ on the paper's population); fixed logged submission order; record per problem the extracted answer, exact match, missing-answer flag, turn count, and the first token of divergence between configurations; $\delta_0$ as the exact-match disagreement rate between each pair of configurations on the subset; $q$ per configuration and $\bar p$ from step 2. Step 2 (about 2 GPU-h, day 2): $m = 16$ sampled episodes per problem at temperature 1.0, top-$p$ 1.0, distinct seeds, batched; record $X_x$, format failures, turn counts. Step 3 (CPU, day 3): raw band shares at $m = 8$ (draws 1-8) and $m = 16$; NPMLE mixing distribution (100-point grid; sensitivity at 50 and 200 points and a three-component Beta mixture) and corrected shares with a problem-level bootstrap (1,000 resamples; sampling error only, model error named) for the bands and for $A$; the kill test with the raw-corrected agreement guard; $\hat A / \hat q$ and $\rho^{*}$; band-edge sensitivity at 0.25 / 0.75; zero-variance flip rates between disjoint $K = 4$ groups (four per problem) and $K = 8$ groups (two per problem); the partition of greedy failures by corrected band, including the $p_x \geq 0.8$ share; the missing-answer versus wrong-answer split of mid-band failures; harness calibrations (split-half band agreement against the binomial prediction; cross-half covariance against the NPMLE variance); the stationary reference $\sum_x (1 - \hat p_x)(1 - (1 - \hat p_x)^{n-1}) / N$ at $n = 100$ as the independent-draw ceiling of a greedy gap. Step 4 (optional, about 6 GPU-h, day 4): steps 1 (batch 64 only) and 2 on the v0.1 sibling; the greedy disagreement set between v0.1 and v0.3 partitioned into strict changes (one side $\geq 0.8$, other $\leq 0.2$), coin-flip cells and argmax flips of settled cells, with the 2609.22547 cross-half residual covariance and its within-model placebo.
killing_experiment.cost_note: H100 at about $2.5-3 per hour; a CPU box with at least 96 GB RAM for the flat index (or +2 GPU-h for faiss-gpu); storage for tens of GB. From the kill report's 8 GPU-h / $20 / 3 days to 8 GPU-h / $35 / 3 days plus download, with the full-dev greedy arm and the sequential alone arm costed.
killing_experiment.kills_if: CL-W46-05 dead (coin-flip clause, under the transfer assumption) if the corrected $\hat A$ has 95% upper bound below $0.5 \cdot 0.62 \cdot \hat q$ on the v0.3 checkpoint, raw and corrected $\hat A$ within 0.03 of each other; at $\hat q = 0.33$ this is $\hat A \lesssim 0.08$ at $N = 1{,}000$. Conditional on the transfer assumption (identifiability). Simulation: the kill fires in 98-100% of replicates in the Sharpening-Tax world (true $A = 0.047$), in 0-2% in the wide-band claim world (true $A = 0.17$, greedy failing on half the mid cells), and in 97-100% in a wide-band world whose greedy decode beats its own samples (greedy failing on 22% or 5% of mid cells; true $A = 0.07$ or 0.02), where the coin-flip cells are not in the gap and the claim is false, as it should. Gate 0 flag on the greedy ruler if $\delta_0 > 5\%$. Informative either way: the band histogram, $A$, $\delta_0$, the empirical misclassification check and the same-checkpoint flip rate are the first such numbers for a public RL'd search agent.

power.method: Simulation (scratchpad redteam-C-W46-14/sim/power.py, python3 -I, 100 replicates per cell; worlds: 'claim' = 45% settled-low Beta(1,15), 20% settled-high Beta(15,1), 35% intermediate Beta(3,3); 'sharp' = 60% / 30% / 10% with Beta(1,25) / Beta(25,1) / Beta(3,3); 'edge' = 40% / 25% / 35% with the intermediate mass at Beta(2,8), the misclassification stress case). Greedy outcome $g_x = \mathbf 1[\mathrm{logit}(p_x) + \varepsilon_x > 0]$, $\varepsilon_x \sim N(0, 1)$: the within-problem correlation between the greedy outcome and $p_x$ is stated and positive (greedy succeeds on most $p > 0.5$ cells and fails on most $p < 0.5$ cells); the design is paired within problem, so between-arm correlation is this one. The kill statistic's SE is the per-problem SD of the posterior indicator $\Pr[\text{mid} \mid X_x]\,(1 - g_x)$ over $\sqrt N$.
power.results: Mean (SD over replicates) of corrected $\hat A$ at $N = 1{,}000$, $m = 16$: claim 0.168 (0.022) against true 0.171; sharp 0.047 (0.012) against 0.047; edge 0.129 (0.027) against 0.120. Raw $m = 8$ overshoots the true $A$ by 0.013 (claim), 0.022 (sharp), 0.030 (edge); raw $m = 16$ by $-0.011$ / $+0.003$ / $-0.005$. Kill rates (threshold $0.31\,\hat q$): sharp 0.98-1.00 at $N = 500$ or $1{,}000$; claim 0.00-0.02; edge 0.01-0.10 (the claim can hold at the edge). $N = 1{,}000$ halves the half-width relative to 500 (0.019 vs 0.026 at $A = 0.1$) at a cost of about one GPU-hour; $m = 16$ over 8 removes the raw bias and gives the split-half rows. Zero-variance flip rate between two disjoint same-checkpoint groups (sim/flips.py): $K = 8$: 0.13-0.15 of all problems and 0.20-0.29 of zero-variance problems in all three worlds; $K = 4$: 0.11-0.15 and 0.14-0.25. Stationary reference at $n = 100$: 0.52-0.59 of $N$, that is 1.5-2.0 times $q$, far above the paper's 0.62, so greedy outcomes across checkpoints are strongly persistent and the stationary reference is a ceiling, not a null. Greedy-advantage sensitivity (sim/power_greedy_sens.py, 40 replicates, $N = 1{,}000$, $m = 16$; latent-logit shift $b = 0 / 1 / 2$ gives $\Pr[g = 0 \mid \text{mid}] = 0.51 / 0.22 / 0.05$): wide-band world true $A$ = 0.166 / 0.071 / 0.019, kill rate 0.00 / 0.97 / 1.00, simulated $q$ = 0.38 / 0.50 / 0.63 against 0.331 in print; sharp world true $A$ = 0.046 / 0.020 / 0.005, kill rate 1.00 throughout.
power.between_arm_correlation: Within-problem pairing of greedy and sampled outcomes; the simulation's latent-logit noise SD 1.0 gives Spearman about 0.7 between $g_x$ and $p_x$. The kill statistic does not depend on this correlation beyond the per-problem variance, because $A$ is a single proportion.

preregistered_surprise.expected: Judgment 0.55: $\hat q$ reported beside 0.331 (decoding unstated in print; no agreement band pre-registered); corrected $f$ (mid band) 0.25-0.40 and $A$ 0.12-0.20, above the kill line 0.10, so the claim is not killed and $\rho^{*}$ is 0.7-1.2; high-band greedy failures under 2% of failures; $\delta_0$ 1-4%; same-checkpoint $K = 8$ flip rate 0.10-0.15 of problems, within a factor two of 2606.10709's cumulative 20%; split-half band agreement within 3 points of the binomial prediction; format failures under a quarter of mid-band failures. Judgment 0.30: $A < 0.08$ (Sharpening-Tax world at 3B after GRPO to near-collapse) and the claim dies for $20. Judgment 0.15: $\delta_0 > 5\%$ or a format artifact dominates the mid band.
preregistered_surprise.field_assumes: Agentic-OPD: greedy for all checkpoint evaluations, the gap read as forgotten capability; Temporal Sampling: greedy 'to minimize variability'; Sharpening Tax: post-trained policies are bimodal (few coin flips), measured base-vs-post-trained at 128 rollouts, not on a checkpoint trajectory; 2606.10709: status flips are partly noise, partly drift, no share.
preregistered_surprise.belief_changing: If $A \geq 0.31 q$ on a converged public checkpoint, the published gap can in principle be at least half coin flips and the greedy forgetting score has no reading without a draw floor; if $A < 0.08$, a 3B GRPO search agent at its own training temperature is near-bimodal and the gap is argmax churn or real drops, which licenses the greedy ruler within the stationary ceiling and kills the lane's coin-flip reading before any training. If the same-checkpoint $K = 8$ flip rate is at or above 0.13, most of 2606.10709's 20% is reproduced with no training at all.

preregistered_reading_2606_10709: 2606.10709 reports that about 20% of unique training queries flip from zero-variance to signal-bearing over training under $K = 8$ groups (cumulative, with drift and noise mixed) and that $K = 4$ yields 17-23% more rescues. This probe reports the fixed-weights analogue: the share of validation problems whose status differs between two disjoint $K = 8$ groups (and between pairs of the four $K = 4$ groups) of the same checkpoint. Reading, written before the run: if the fixed-weights $K = 8$ flip share is at or above 0.13 of problems (0.20 of zero-variance problems), the published 20% is within what one resampling of a fixed policy produces and 'as the policy drifts' is unsupported without a split; if it is below 0.05, drift carries their figure. Caveats carried: their population is training queries on Qwen3-1.7B/4B, ours is HotpotQA dev on Qwen2.5-3B-Instruct; their count is cumulative over many resamplings, ours is one pair, so ours is a lower bound on the noise-only share.

scorecard.target_value: In print: Agentic-OPD sec. 2 ('greedy decoding for all checkpoint evaluations'), sec. 4.3 (60/45 of 2,000, 'describes consolidation behavior'), sec. 5 ('reliably recovered' as a next step); Temporal Sampling sec. 2.2 (greedy to minimize variability); 2609.22547 Limitations ('multi-turn agentic or tool-use settings remains open'); 2606.10709 sec. 3.3 ('a stochastic observation'). Who pays: whoever is about to buy a consolidation stage on the strength of a greedy gap; authors of forgetting scores; anyone selecting a checkpoint from a run.

impact_ceiling.floor: A four-number note ($q$, $f$, $A$, $\delta_0$) with the misclassification check for one public RL'd search agent, cited by C-W46-13 and the next forgetting paper. Requires steps 0-3. Judgment 0.6.
impact_ceiling.middle: The kill fires or the pool clears with margin, deciding for $30 whether C-W46-13's 150 GPU-h are spent; with step 4, the first three-way split with a draw floor of a between-policy greedy disagreement set. Judgment 0.3.
impact_ceiling.ceiling: None beyond C-W46-13's: this is its step 0.

scorecard.relevance: Narasimhan route and any RL group: direct (how many draws a checkpoint table needs; what a 3B GRPO policy's success-probability histogram looks like at its training temperature). L1: direct (serving floor of greedy agent tables). Industry: direct for consolidation buyers. Systems route, L4, L5: zero. Jacob's edge: the pool bound, the misclassification matrix and the NPMLE inversion are napkin statistics; a first result in a weekend.
scorecard.kill_probe: This probe: about 6 GPU-h (12 with step 4), $30-50, 3-4 days; kills CL-W46-05's coin-flip clause if the corrected $\hat A$ upper bound is below $0.31\,\hat q$.
scorecard.density_and_ownership: Kill search 2026-11-15: no fetched source splits a greedy checkpoint gap by a draw floor; the direction is in print (2606.10709; 2609.22547's placebo); about one checkpoint-forgetting paper a month. Occupied: the greedy table and recovery count (Agentic-OPD); the oscillation reading (Temporal Sampling); bimodalisation at 128 rollouts base-vs-post (Sharpening Tax); temperature-0 serving variance in general (2602.07150). Owners of the data: Temporal Sampling authors (64 samples on 8 checkpoints), Agentic-OPD authors (100 checkpoints), Search-R1 authors (training logs). Race flag carried from the kill report.
scorecard.why_now: As above; the public checkpoint and harness make the pool bound free of training.
scorecard.register: A one-sided kill and a noise-floor measurement; the cheapest first move under CL-W46-05. It is not the G-study (no checkpoint facet), not a test of the strict-drop clause, not a verdict on forgetting, and not a claim about the paper's own run: it bounds the claim's coin-flip clause through a stated transfer assumption.

identifiability: Random given: one question, the fixed v0.3 weights, the fixed retriever (E5 over the 2018 dump, deterministic given the query string), the Table 1 template, four turns, top-3 passages, temperature 1.0 and top-$p$ 1.0, the pinned vLLM build. The environment is deterministic given the action sequence, so there is no luck term; $p_x$ is the policy's and belongs to the (weights, temperature) pair; the binomial residual $p_x(1 - p_x)/m$ is the protocol's and is removed by the NPMLE inversion. Whose temperature: the training temperature (Search-R1 sec. 4.3), which is where GRPO's groups were scored, so a coin-flip band at 1.0 is the band the optimiser saw. At $T = 0$ the party has zero decision variance by construction; $\delta_0$ is a property of the serving stack (batch composition is the axis), not of the policy. Property of the thing or of the protocol: the raw band share is protocol-dependent through $m$ (the misclassification matrix says by how much); the corrected share is a property of the policy at the stated temperature. Transfer assumption, stated: the claim's run is Agentic-OPD's HotpotQA-only preliminary (best checkpoint of 100, greedy validation on a 10% split of HotpotQA train); the probe's checkpoint is the Search-R1 NQ+HotpotQA run's released checkpoint, which the paper's App. B.2 rule makes either the final or 'the most recent stable checkpoint according to the training reward curve', evaluated on HotpotQA dev; $|G|$ is imported as $\rho q N$ with $\rho = 0.62$ from $U_{\geq 3}$ against the final checkpoint (the claim's $U_{\geq 1}$ against the best is a different ratio; sensitivity rows at 0.5 and 0.8). The released checkpoint is 'either the final checkpoint at step 600 or the last checkpoint prior to collapse' (2505.15117 App. G.1), chosen on the training reward curve, not the best-validation checkpoint; the kill is therefore conditional on that checkpoint standing for the recipe's best checkpoints in band width, which 2610.01509 App. C.2 makes plausible in the direction favouring the claim (less-trained policies keep more intermediate mass) and which only C-W46-13 or the data owners can test. The retriever is the flat E5 index (exact search, deterministic given the query string). Re-open trigger if the kill fires: a run whose best checkpoint keeps at least $0.62 q$ of its problems in the coin-flip pool.
positioning_note: Solo: an afternoon on one GPU plus a retrieval server; nobody is needed. Lab: the same reading on the Agentic-OPD authors' 100 checkpoints or the Temporal Sampling authors' 64 samples is a day and decides both clauses; from the solo position the strict-drop clause waits for C-W46-13 or a continuation run.

objections.persona: theory; checklist:2026-10-20 (each pre-registered outcome informative); checklist:2026-11-08 (write the decomposition identity before a share headline)
objections.objection: The kill imports $|G| = \rho q N$ with $\rho = 0.62$, but 0.62 is $|U_{\geq 3}| / |Q_{\mathrm{final}}| - 1$ (4,553 / 2,808) and the claim's gap is $U_{\geq 1} \setminus Q_{\mathrm{best}}$; $U_{\geq 1} \supseteq U_{\geq 3}$, so the claim's $\rho$ is larger than 0.62 by an unknown amount (the record's own stationary ceiling puts the independent-draw ratio at 1.5-2.0 of $q$). A larger $\rho$ raises the kill line $0.5 \rho q$, so the kill at 0.62 is conservative for the claim, but the 'survives to C-W46-13 if $\hat A - 1.96\,\mathrm{SE} \geq 0.31\,\hat q$' reading is not a support reading at all: at $\rho = 1.0$ the pool must be $0.5 q$ and at $\rho = 1.2$, $0.6 q$, and the record's expected $A = 0.12$-0.20 against $q = 0.33$ (ratio 0.36-0.6) sits inside that range. The positive outcome is therefore 'indeterminate' for most plausible $\rho$, and the sensitivity rows at 0.5 and 0.8 do not cover the plausible range.
objections.evidence: 2611.12799 sec. 2 (2,808 vs 4,553 is $U_{\geq 3}$ against the final checkpoint; card weakest_component); sim/flips.py stationary reference 0.52-0.59 of $N$ = 1.5-2.0 $q$; v2 statement and kills_if; argument (set inclusion $U_{\geq 1} \supseteq U_{\geq 3}$).
objections.answer: Answered, with the support reading rewritten. The kill is valid for every $\rho \geq 0.62$ because it is an inequality in the conservative direction (a larger gap needs more coin flips), and 0.62 is the only gap ratio in print for this recipe, so it stays the pre-registered kill line. The objection is right that 'pool sufficient at $\rho = 0.62$' is not support: the record now reports the ratio $\hat A / \hat q$ with its band and the break-even gap ratio $\rho^{*} = 2 \hat A / \hat q$, read as 'the pool can fill half of any gap up to $\rho^{*}$ of the best set'; the claim survives to C-W46-13 only in the sense that it is not killed, and the record says so in those words. The sensitivity rows become $\rho \in \{0.62, 1.0, 1.5\}$; the paper's own $U_{\geq 1}$ count is not in its text, so the letter to the Agentic-OPD authors (new step 0c) asks for $|U_{\geq 1}|$ and $|Q_{\mathrm{best}}|$, which fixes $\rho$ for free if answered. The one-sidedness was already in the v2 statement ('never that the clause holds'); what changes is that the positive outcome is labelled 'not killed; $\rho^{*}$ reported' rather than 'survives'.

objections.persona: theory; professor; checklist: regime stated; checklist:2026-11-08 (name the shipped level in the headline or fail Gate 0's protocol clause)
objections.objection: The probe's checkpoint is the wrong object twice and the record's transfer assumption does not bridge it. (i) The claim's cell is 'the best checkpoint' of a HotpotQA-only run with 100 checkpoints (2611.12799 sec. 2); the released v0.3 checkpoint is, by the recipe owners' own rule, 'either the final checkpoint at step 600 or the last checkpoint prior to collapse' of an NQ+HotpotQA run (2505.15117 App. G.1), and the first paper says 'GRPO leads to reward collapse after training for many steps' (2503.09516v5 sec. 5.1): a last-before-collapse checkpoint selected by eye on the reward curve has no reason to share its band width with a best-validation checkpoint of a different run. (ii) The record's 'the kill is valid for any run whose best checkpoint has a band no wider than this checkpoint's' is not an inequality anyone has established; it is the thing in question. So the kill, if it fires, kills 'CL-W46-05 instantiated on v0.3', not the claim about Agentic-OPD's run, and a survival says nothing about that run either.
objections.evidence: 2505.15117 App. G.1 (fetched 2026-11-16, redteam-C-W46-14/fetch/searchr1_v03.txt: 'Each model is trained for up to 600 steps, with early stopping triggered if training collapse is observed based on the reward curve. For the results reported in Table 1, we use either the final checkpoint at step 600 or the last checkpoint prior to collapse'); 2503.09516v5 sec. 5.1 and App. B.2 (fetch/searchr1.txt); 2611.12799 sec. 2; v2 identifiability.
objections.answer: Answered on the claim's scope, conceded on the bridge. The claim's headline says 'a Search-R1-recipe GRPO run (Qwen2.5-3B-Instruct, HotpotQA, four turns)', indefinite article: it is a statement about runs of this recipe at this size, and the released v0.3 checkpoint is a run of this recipe at this size (NQ+HotpotQA training, HotpotQA in-domain, four turns, group 5, temperature 1), so a pool too small on it is a counterexample to the claim as written and forces the narrowing the record now pre-registers: if the kill fires, the claim is parked with the re-open trigger 'a run whose best checkpoint keeps at least $2 \cdot 0.31 q$ of its problems in the coin-flip pool', and CL-W46-05's headline is marked as needing a run qualifier before it can be re-filed. Conceded: the sentence 'valid for any run whose best checkpoint has a band no wider than this checkpoint's' is a restatement of the assumption, not an argument; it is replaced by the plain statement that the kill is conditional on the recipe's final-or-last-stable checkpoint being representative of the recipe's best checkpoints in band width, which 2610.01509 App. C.2 (smaller and less-trained policies keep more intermediate mass) makes plausible in the direction that favours the claim (a best-validation checkpoint earlier in training should have a band at least as wide), and which only C-W46-13 or the data owners can test. Added to step 0: read the public wandb log of the 3B-it GRPO v0.3 run (README links it) for the number of steps completed and whether the run collapsed, and record which rule produced the release.

objections.objection: Known idea with new words. Every GRPO practitioner has the per-prompt group-variance histogram of a 3B policy at temperature 1 on their dashboard; 2610.01509 measured the per-task success-rate histogram at 128 rollouts on 14 base-post pairs; 2606.10709 built a recipe on the fact that many search-agent queries are signal-bearing at $K = 5$-8; greedy-versus-sample disagreement is the pass@1-versus-greedy folklore. The probe's deliverables are that histogram, a greedy agreement rate and a serving-noise rate for one checkpoint. The only part not in print is the inequality 'coin-flip gap members are at most the mid-band greedy failures', which is arithmetic. What would a reviewer cite from this? If the answer is 'a histogram', the probe is a service to the lane, not a probe of a claim (CL-W45-04 lesson).

The register already says 'the cheapest first move under CL-W46-05 ... its step 0' and the floor scenario (judgment 0.6) is a four-number note; the probe is not offered as the claim's surprise. Its job under Gate 1 is to decide for $30 whether C-W46-13's 150 GPU-h are spent, and it can do that in one direction (objection 1). Two of its readouts are not folklore and not in print for any RL'd agent: (a) the serving floor $\delta_0$ of a greedy agent table beside a published recovery count (2602.07150 measured it for SWE-bench scaffolds, not for a checkpoint table; Agentic-OPD and Temporal Sampling report none), and (b) the share of greedy failures on cells the policy solves with $p \geq 0.8$ (the argmax losing to its own mode in a four-turn loop), which no fetched source reports and which the five-way partition (objection 7) needs. Sharpening Tax's histograms are base-versus-post-trained on math at 128 rollouts; its own limitation is that the analysis is 'observational rather than interventional' and its RL runs pick the best-validation checkpoint without a table; the agentic setting is 'open' in 2609.22547's words. The reviewer would cite the kill (if it fires: 'a public 3B GRPO search agent has too few coin-flip failures to fill half of a published forgetting gap') or the floor. Classification accepted as killing; the answer stands because the probe's value was never claimed to be novelty.

objections.persona: systems; checklist:2026-10-20 (open the README's data layout before costing an arm); checklist:2026-10-08 (deterministic sandboxes: name the environment)
objections.objection: The retriever is the environment and the probe has not pinned it. The recipe owners trained and evaluated with 'E5 (exact)' flat indexing (2505.15117 App. G.1); their docs offer HNSW64 on CPU as the cheap path and say it 'may not be as accurate as flat indexing, especially when the number of retrieved passages is small' (top-3 here). Switching to HNSW changes the retrieved passages, hence $p_x$ and the greedy path, and the comparison to Table 3's 0.331 is lost. Flat search on GPU needs the index resident (the README downloads e5_Flat.index in parts; its size is not stated in the docs); co-locating a 65-GB-class index with the 3B model on one 80 GB GPU is not budgeted, and CPU flat search over about 21M passages at 768 dimensions is a dense matrix-vector product per query that the record has not timed. Also the corpus and index download is tens of GB and the 'days: 3' line starts the clock after it.
objections.evidence: repo docs/retriever.md lines 15-17, 52-56, 83-84 (fetched 2026-11-16, redteam-C-W46-14/fetch/repo_retriever.md); README lines 104-111 ('cat $save_path/part_* > $save_path/e5_Flat.index'); 2505.15117 App. G.1 'We adopt E5 (exact) as the retriever and return the top-3 passages (each contains about 200 tokens)'.
objections.answer: Answered by pinning and costing. Pre-registered: the flat E5 index ('E5 (exact)', the training retriever), never HNSW; served on CPU with faiss (the index file size is read at step 0; about 21M passages at 768 dimensions in float32 is about 65 GB, judgment, so a machine with at least 96 GB RAM), at about 16 GFLOP per query a 32-core box does one query in roughly 0.1-0.3 s, and the probe issues at most 4 searches per episode times about 20,000 episodes (steps 1-2) = 80,000 queries, 3-7 CPU-hours, overlapped with decoding; a second GPU for faiss-gpu is the faster alternative and is costed as 2 extra GPU-h. The download (tens of GB) is day 1 and is now written into the days line (3 days plus the download). The retriever's determinism given the query string (flat exact search, fixed index) is part of the conditioning set and is stated in identifiability.

objections.persona: systems; checklist:2026-10-10 (temperature-0 through an API is not a deterministic arm; budget the deterministic stack or drop the arm); checklist:2026-11-08 (hold chunked prefill, prefix cache and run length fixed in cross-engine comparisons)
objections.objection: 'Three batch compositions' is not an operational definition under vLLM's continuous batching: the set of co-resident requests changes at every decode step, so 'batch of 16' and 'batch of 64' are schedulers with max_num_seqs caps, not compositions, and the 'alone' arm is the only reproducible one. $\delta_0$ between two scheduler caps measures one serving stack against itself; the paper's tables were produced by verl's vLLM rollout worker at its own version, dtype and chunked-prefill settings, so our $\delta_0$ is a lower bound on cross-server disagreement, not the floor under the paper's 60/45. And the 'alone' arm is sequential: 1,000 episodes x up to 4 turns x (prefill of 1-2k tokens, about 150 generated tokens, a retrieval round trip) is 3-5 hours of wall-clock on one GPU, most of it idle, which the 'about 3 GPU-h' for step 1 just covers.
objections.evidence: 2602.07150 abstract (SD above 1.5 points at $T = 0$); checklist 2026-10-10 ('80 unique completions of 1,000 at temperature 0; batch-invariant kernels cost 1.6-2.1x'); vLLM continuous batching (argument); v2 killing_experiment.design step 1.
objections.answer: Answered by defining the arms operationally and re-labelling what $\delta_0$ is. Arms: (alone) max_num_seqs = 1, requests submitted one at a time, the reproducible reference; (16) and (64) max_num_seqs = 16 and 64 with a fixed, logged submission order and prefix caching off, so each arm is a named scheduler configuration and the co-resident set per step is logged, not controlled. $\delta_0$ is defined as the exact-match disagreement rate between (alone) and each capped arm, and between the two capped arms, under one pinned vLLM build, bf16, chunked prefill off; the record states that it is a within-stack floor and a lower bound on the cross-server disagreement that the paper's tables carry (which would need the verl rollout worker at the paper's version; not budgeted, named as the lab-position extension). Wall-clock: the alone arm at about 4 s per turn x 4 turns x 1,000 episodes is about 4.5 hours on one GPU; step 1 is re-costed at about 5 GPU-h (alone 4.5, capped arms 0.5), the whole probe at about 8 GPU-h without step 4.

objections.objection: The anchor $q = 0.331$ has no decoding attached: the paper text never says how Table 3 was decoded (zero occurrences of 'greedy'), the repository's reference inference script samples at temperature 0.7 (`do_sample=True, temperature=0.7`), and the training pipeline's validation decoding lives in the verl config the record has not read. 'Within 0.05 of 0.331' therefore compares a greedy number with a number of unknown decoding. Separately, 'format failure' has no operational definition: the reward's `extract_solution` takes the last `<answer>...</answer>` match and scores 0 otherwise, and the record does not say whether an episode that exhausts the four-turn budget without an answer is a format failure, a wrong answer or a forced final answer.

objections.answer: Answered by pre-registering both. (i) $q$ is reported three ways: greedy (alone arm), greedy (batch 64), and the mean of the sixteen sampled outcomes $\bar p = N^{-1} \sum_x \hat p_x$ at temperature 1; the in-print 0.331 is labelled 'decoding unstated in both papers; reference script samples at 0.7' and sits beside all three, with no pre-registered agreement band on it (the 'within 0.05' expectation is withdrawn as unsupported, the kill does not use it: the kill uses the probe's own $\hat q$).
